nodes.name: JunctionTableError
nodes.body_text: class JunctionTableError(ValueError): pass

nodes.name: parse_alignment_spec
nodes.body_text: def parse_alignment_spec(text): parts = text.split(":", 2) if len(parts) != 3 or parts[0] not in SOURCE_THRESHOLDS or \ parts[1] not in ("uf=true", "uf=false"): raise JunctionTableError( f"--alignment must be SOURCE:uf=BOOL:PATH with SOURCE in " f"{sorted(SOURCE_THRESHOLDS)}; got {text!r}") source, uf_text, path = parts uf = uf_text == "uf=true" if source == "HiFi" and uf: raise JunctionTableError("HiFi (splice:hq) has no -uf mode; uf must be false") return source, uf, Path(path)

nodes.name: collect_junctions
nodes.body_text: def collect_junctions(alignment_path, uf, windows, samtools="samtools"): """Yield (junction_key, read_name) for accepted reads; return QC counters. junction_key = (chrom, intron_start0, intron_end0, tx_strand) with 0-based INCLUSIVE endpoints (parse_sam introns are 1-based inclusive; converted here once). Junctions with unknown strand or outside every panel window are counted in QC, never tabulated. """ groups = defaultdict(list) for line in ES.sam_lines(str(alignment_path), samtools): aln = ES.parse_sam(line) if aln is not None: groups[aln.read].append(aln) qc = Counter() pairs = [] for read in sorted(groups): records = groups[read] rejection = ES.alignment_rejection(records) if rejection: qc["rejected:" + rejection] += 1 continue aln = next(r for r in records if not r.flag & (4 | 0x900)) strand = ES.transcript_strand(aln, uf=uf) qc["accepted_reads"] += 1 for start1, end1 in aln.introns: start0, end0 = start1 - 1, end1 - 1 if strand is None: qc["junctions_strand_unknown"] += 1 continue if not mvp_windows.junction_within_windows(aln.contig, start0, end0, windows): qc["junctions_outside_panel_windows"] += 1 continue qc["junctions_in_panel_windows"] += 1 pairs.append(((aln.contig, start0, end0, strand), read)) qc["raw_reads"] = len(groups) return pairs, qc

nodes.name: build_table
nodes.body_text: def build_table(alignments, windows, samtools="samtools"): reads_by_source = {source: defaultdict(set) for source in SOURCE_THRESHOLDS} qc = {} seen = set() for source, uf, path in alignments: identity = Path(path).resolve() if identity in seen: raise JunctionTableError("duplicate alignment input") seen.add(identity) pairs, counters = collect_junctions(path, uf, windows, samtools) for key, read in pairs: reads_by_source[source][key].add((str(path), read)) qc[f"{source}:{path}"] = dict(sorted(counters.items())) keys = sorted(set(reads_by_source["ONT"]) | set(reads_by_source["HiFi"])) rows = [] for key in keys: n_ont = len(reads_by_source["ONT"].get(key, ())) n_hifi = len(reads_by_source["HiFi"].get(key, ())) supported = (n_hifi >= SOURCE_THRESHOLDS["HiFi"] or n_ont >= SOURCE_THRESHOLDS["ONT"]) chrom, start0, end0, strand = key rows.append({"chrom": chrom, "intron_start0": start0, "intron_end0": end0, "tx_strand": strand, "n_ONT": n_ont, "n_HiFi": n_hifi, "supported": supported}) return rows, qc

nodes.name: write_table
nodes.body_text: def write_table(rows, out_path): with open(out_path, "w") as f: f.write("\t".join(HEADER) + "\n") for row in rows: f.write("\t".join(str(row[c]).lower() if c == "supported" else str(row[c]) for c in HEADER) + "\n")

nodes.name: read_table
nodes.body_text: def read_table(path): """Load a table written by write_table, fail-closed on schema drift.""" rows = [] with open(path) as f: header = tuple(f.readline().rstrip("\n").split("\t")) if header != HEADER: raise JunctionTableError(f"junction table header mismatch: {header!r}") for line in f: fields = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t") if len(fields) != len(HEADER): raise JunctionTableError("junction table row width mismatch") if fields[6] not in ("true", "false"): raise JunctionTableError("supported must be true/false") rows.append({"chrom": fields[0], "intron_start0": int(fields[1]), "intron_end0": int(fields[2]), "tx_strand": fields[3], "n_ONT": int(fields[4]), "n_HiFi": int(fields[5]), "supported": fields[6] == "true"}) keys = set() for row in rows: key = tuple(row[c] for c in HEADER[:4]) if (key in keys or row['tx_strand'] not in ('+', '-') or not 0 <= row['intron_start0'] <= row['intron_end0'] or min(row['n_ONT'], row['n_HiFi']) < 0 or row['supported'] != (row['n_ONT'] >= 3 or row['n_HiFi'] >= 2)): raise JunctionTableError('invalid, duplicate, or inconsistent junction row') keys.add(key) return rows

nodes.name: main
nodes.body_text: def main(argv=None): parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__) parser.add_argument("--alignment", action="append", required=True, metavar="SOURCE:uf=BOOL:PATH", help="repeatable; SOURCE is ONT or HiFi; uf must state " "the audited -uf decision explicitly") parser.add_argument("--panels", required=True, type=Path) parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path) parser.add_argument("--qc-out", required=True, type=Path) parser.add_argument("--samtools", default="samtools") args = parser.parse_args(argv) expected = mvp_windows.PANEL_SHA256 loci = mvp_windows.load_panel(args.panels, expected_sha256=expected) windows = mvp_windows.windows_by_chromosome(loci) alignments = [parse_alignment_spec(text) for text in args.alignment] rows, qc = build_table(alignments, windows, args.samtools) write_table(rows, args.out) qc_report = { "panel_sha256": expected, "panel_sha256_is_frozen": expected == mvp_windows.PANEL_SHA256, "thresholds": SOURCE_THRESHOLDS, "counts_are": "reads (UMI status unknown; never molecules)", "scorer": "59_evidence_support.py (sha256 " + hashlib.sha256((_SCRIPTS / "59_evidence_support.py") .read_bytes()).hexdigest() + ")", "restriction": "junction contained in a 30,720-nt panel evaluation window", "per_input": qc, "junctions": len(rows), "supported_junctions": sum(r["supported"] for r in rows), } args.qc_out.write_text(json.dumps(qc_report, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n") return 0

nodes.name: selected_provenance
nodes.body_text: def selected_provenance(con, chrom, start, end): """Same independent block/endpoint predicates as rasterise_est, no RN join.""" def records(sql, params): cursor = con.execute(sql, params) names = [col[0] for col in cursor.description] return [dict(zip(names, row)) for row in cursor.fetchall()] policy = "m.excluded AND m.cause='heldout_locus' AND m.primary_count>0" blocks = records(f'''SELECT b.* FROM est_block b JOIN est_molecule m USING(molecule_id) WHERE b.chrom=? AND b.start0<? AND b.end0>? AND {policy} ORDER BY b.molecule_id,b.start0,b.end0''', [chrom, end, start]) junctions = records(f'''SELECT j.* FROM est_junction j JOIN est_molecule m USING(molecule_id) WHERE j.chrom=? AND ((j.donor0>=? AND j.donor0<?) OR (j.acceptor0>=? AND j.acceptor0<?)) AND {policy} ORDER BY j.molecule_id,j.donor0,j.acceptor0''', [chrom, start, end, start, end]) grouped = {} for kind, rows in [('blocks', blocks), ('junctions', junctions)]: for row in rows: grouped.setdefault(row['molecule_id'], {'blocks': [], 'junctions': []})[kind].append(row) # ponytail: two metadata lookups per selected molecule; batch if real-panel profiling requires it. for mid, geometry in sorted(grouped.items()): molecule = records('SELECT * FROM est_molecule WHERE molecule_id=?', [mid]) require(len(molecule) == 1, 'ambiguous molecule identity') members = records('SELECT * FROM est_member WHERE molecule_id=? ORDER BY member', [mid]) require(members, 'selected molecule lacks member provenance') yield dict(molecule=molecule[0], members=members, **geometry)

nodes.name: fasta_sequences
nodes.body_text: def fasta_sequences(path): """Stream contigs without trusting or creating a FASTA index.""" seen, chrom, parts = set(), None, [] with Path(path).open() as handle: for line in handle: if line.startswith('>'): if chrom is not None: yield chrom, ''.join(parts) chrom = line[1:].split()[0] require(chrom not in seen, 'duplicate FASTA contig') seen.add(chrom) parts = [] elif line.strip(): require(chrom is not None, 'FASTA sequence before header') parts.append(line.strip()) if chrom is not None: yield chrom, ''.join(parts)

def prepare(input_path, out): out = Path(out).absolute() if out.exists() or out.is_symlink(): raise FileExistsError(out) request_identity = file_identity(input_path) payload = read_json(input_path) loci, authority, identities, evidence = preflight(payload) identities.append(request_identity) require(not Path(str(evidence) + '.wal').exists(), 'evidence DB has WAL') unchanged(identities) out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False) outputs, rows = [], {} def artifact(path): identity = file_identity(path) outputs.append(identity) return {'path': str(path.relative_to(out)), 'sha256': identity['sha256'], 'bytes': identity['size']} with duckdb.connect(str(evidence), config={'access_mode': 'READ_ONLY', 'threads': 1}) as con: for chrom, bases in fasta_sequences(payload['fasta']): for index, locus in enumerate(loci): if locus.chromosome != chrom: continue start, end = w.evaluation_window(locus, len(bases)) sequence = bases[start:end] tracks = panel_tracks(con, sequence, chrom, start) require(tracks.dtype == np.float16 and tracks.shape == (30720, 8), 'invalid track tensor') require(np.isfinite(tracks).all(), 'nonfinite tracks') prefix = out / f'{index:02d}' # no gene identifiers in filesystem paths track_path = prefix.with_suffix('.npy') with track_path.open('xb') as handle: np.save(handle, tracks, allow_pickle=False) track = dict(artifact(track_path), dtype='float16', shape=[30720, 8]) sequence_path = prefix.with_suffix('.fa') with sequence_path.open('x') as handle: handle.write(f'>{locus.gene_id} {chrom}:{start}-{end} genomic_forward
{sequence}
') provenance_path = prefix.with_suffix('.jsonl') count = 0 with provenance_path.open('x') as handle: for record in selected_provenance(con, chrom, start, end): handle.write(canonical(record)) count += 1 biological = np.count_nonzero(tracks[:, :7], axis=0).tolist() rows[index] = dict(gene_id=locus.gene_id, window=[chrom, start, end], sequence_sha256=hashlib.sha256(sequence.encode('ascii')).hexdigest(), sequence=artifact(sequence_path), track=track, provenance=artifact(provenance_path), selected_molecule_count=count, biological_nonzero_per_channel=biological, availability_nonzero=int(np.count_nonzero(tracks[:, 7])), zero_biological_support=not any(biological)) require(len(rows) == len(loci), 'panel chromosome absent from FASTA') manifest = dict(schema_version=1, purpose='est_mvp_panel_inputs_not_training', training_eligible=False, orientation='genomic_forward', population='excluded_heldout', keep_fraction=1, source='EST', seeds=[1, 2, 3], aug_seeds=[20260915, 20260916, 20260917], seed_tracks_identical=True, off_policy='zeros_like(on); same sequence/window', zero_support_policy='report_not_fail', inputs=identities, authority=authority, rasterizer=file_identity(mvp_tracks.__file__), packages={'numpy': np.__version__, 'duckdb': duckdb.__version__}, loci=[rows[i] for i in range(len(loci))]) unchanged(identities + outputs) require(not Path(str(evidence) + '.wal').exists(), 'evidence DB WAL appeared') manifest_path = out / 'manifest.json' with manifest_path.open('x') as handle: handle.write(canonical(manifest)) published = file_identity(manifest_path) unchanged(identities + outputs + [published]) require(not Path(str(evidence) + '.wal').exists(), 'evidence DB WAL appeared') with (out / 'COMPLETE').open('x') as handle: handle.write(published['sha256'] + '
') return manifest

nodes.name: frozen_reference
nodes.body_text: def frozen_reference(fasta, reference): """Read authority from an existing immutable git object, never the working copy.""" proc = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(ROOT), 'show', f'{AUTHORITY_COMMIT}:{AUTHORITY_PATH}'], check=True, capture_output=True) rows = list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(proc.stdout.decode()), delimiter='\t')) rows = [r for r in rows if r['species_id'] == 'Athaliana'] require(len(rows) == 1, 'missing/ambiguous frozen Athaliana manifest row') bound = {} for name, path in [('fasta', fasta), ('gff', reference)]: digest = hashlib.md5() with Path(path).open('rb') as f: for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b''): digest.update(block) require(digest.hexdigest() == rows[0][name + '_md5'], f'frozen {name} identity mismatch') bound[name] = file_identity(path) return {'commit': AUTHORITY_COMMIT, 'manifest': AUTHORITY_PATH, 'manifest_sha256': hashlib.sha256(proc.stdout).hexdigest(), 'files': bound}

nodes.name: verify_training_code

No scoring-runtime comparison. for name in required_packages - {'duckdb'}: require(packages[name] == metadata['runtime_packages'][name], 'code/runtime package mismatch') implementation = metadata['initialization_audit']['audit']['implementation'] runtime_path = Path(implementation['b5_runtime.py']['path']) require(runtime_path.is_absolute() and runtime_path.parts[-4:] == ('src', 'transgenic', 'training', 'b5_runtime.py'), 'invalid bound training checkout path') root = runtime_path.parents[3].resolve(strict=True) # Same closure as mvp_cli_runtime._expected_code_files, evaluated in the # historical training checkout. Additional scoring-checkout files are irrelevant. expected = {str(path) for path in (root/'src/transgenic').rglob('*.py')} expected.add(str(root/'train/train_HyenaTransgenic_MVP.py')) require(set(files) == expected, 'consumed code manifest must match exact bound training source closure') require(all(str(Path(path).resolve(strict=True)) == path for path in files), 'noncanonical consumed code path') identities = [check_file(path, {'sha256': digest}) for path, digest in files.items()] for name, relative in [('b5_runtime.py', 'src/transgenic/training/b5_runtime.py'), ('configuration_transgenic.py', 'src/transgenic/model/configuration_transgenic.py')]: path = str(root/relative) require(implementation[name] == {'path': path, 'sha256': files.get(path)}, 'initialization implementation/code binding mismatch') # Reconstruct semantics only with the same project-owned implementation. # Do not import/execute arbitrary files from a supplied historical checkout. from transgenic.training import weights_init as wi for module, relative in [(wi, 'src/transgenic/training/weights_init.py'), (wi.b5_runtime, 'src/transgenic/training/b5_runtime.py'), (wi.configuration_transgenic, 'src/transgenic/model/configuration_transgenic.py')]: require(files.get(str(root/relative)) == w.sha256_file(module.__file__), 'unsupported historical semantic implementation; reviewed verifier adapter required') return identities

nodes.body_text: def read_gff(path): """Strict preflight around the existing half-open GFF parser; never repair data.""" genes, transcripts, features = {}, {}, [] gff3_header = False with Path(path).open() as f: for line in f: if line.rstrip('\r\n') == '##gff-version 3': gff3_header = True if not line.strip() or line.startswith('#'): continue cols = line.rstrip('\n').split('\t') require(len(cols) == 9, 'malformed GFF: expected nine columns') chrom, _, kind, start, end, _, strand, phase, attrs = cols require(int(start) >= 1 and int(end) >= int(start) and strand in ('+', '-'), 'invalid GFF coordinates/strand') fields = [a.split('=', 1) for a in attrs.split(';') if a] require(all(len(a) == 2 for a in fields) and len(dict(fields)) == len(fields), 'malformed GFF attributes') attrs = dict(fields) require(all(key == key.strip() and not any(c.isspace() for c in key) for key in attrs), 'noncanonical GFF attribute key') for key in ('ID', 'Parent'): if key in attrs: identifiers = attrs[key].split(',') if key == 'Parent' else [attrs[key]] require(all(re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+', value) for value in identifiers) and len(identifiers) == len(set(identifiers)), 'noncanonical GFF ID/Parent') span = (chrom, int(start) - 1, int(end), strand) if kind == 'gene': gid = attrs.get('ID') require(gid and gid not in genes, 'missing/duplicate GFF gene ID') genes[gid] = span elif kind in ('mRNA', 'transcript'): tid, parent = attrs.get('ID'), attrs.get('Parent') require(tid and tid not in transcripts and parent in genes, 'missing/duplicate transcript or unordered/orphan gene') transcripts[tid] = (parent, span) elif kind in ('exon', 'CDS', 'five_prime_UTR', 'three_prime_UTR'): require(kind != 'CDS' or phase in ('0', '1', '2'), 'invalid CDS phase') for parent in attrs.get('Parent', '').split(','): require(parent in transcripts, 'orphan/unordered GFF feature') features.append((parent, span)) else: raise ValueError(f'unsupported GFF feature {kind}; no silent omission') require(genes or gff3_header, 'completed empty prediction requires explicit ##gff-version 3 header') def contained(child, parent): return child[0] == parent[0] and child[3] == parent[3] and parent[1] <= child[1] < child[2] <= parent[2] for parent, span in transcripts.values(): require(contained(span, genes[parent]), 'transcript outside parent gene') for parent, span in features: require(contained(span, transcripts[parent][1]), 'feature outside transcript') parsed = legacy_module('07_selfconsistency_stats.py').load_gff(str(path)) require(set(parsed) == set(genes), 'GFF parser gene inventory changed') for gid, gene in parsed.items(): require(set(gene['transcripts']) == {tid for tid, (parent, _) in transcripts.items() if parent == gid}, 'GFF parser transcript inventory changed') for gene in parsed.values(): require(gene['transcripts'], 'GFF gene has no transcripts; only a header-only file represents zero predictions') for tx in gene['transcripts'].values(): require(tx['exons'], 'explicit exon geometry required; CDS is not an exon substitute') for key in ('exons', 'cdss'): tx[key].sort() require(all(a[1] < b[0] for a, b in zip(tx[key], tx[key][1:])), 'duplicate/overlapping/adjacent GFF segments') require(all(any(a <= c < d <= b for a, b in tx['exons']) for c, d in tx['cdss']), 'CDS outside exons') return parsed

nodes.name: mvp_score.py
nodes.body_text: #!/usr/bin/env python3 """CPU MVP statistics from caller-supplied counts and final eval-pair JSONL. Input JSON: pairs maps '1','2','3' to final deduplicated JSONL paths; loci is 50 records {gene_id, seeds: {'1': {'off': counts, 'on': counts}, ...}}. counts: f1_tp, f1_predicted, f1_reference (GFFCompare v0.12.6 restricted transcript counts; monoexonic exact CDS), and optionally precision_tp, predicted, recall_tp, supported (exact junction counts). All are integers. Structural counts must be present everywhere or nowhere, never filled as zero for missing evidence. F1 is percentage points; P/R are fractions. This adapter does not decode models or claim to run GFFCompare. Pair paths must identify distinct files, but filenames and seed keys do not prove distinct runs. API and CLI outputs mark pair/run provenance UNVERIFIED and three-seed identity/policy unverified until anchored producer receipts are integrated. """ import argparse import json import math import sys from pathlib import Path sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / 'src')) from transgenic.evidence import mvp_bootstrap as b, mvp_windows as w if __name__ == '__main__': raise SystemExit(main())

nodes.name: predicted_junctions
nodes.body_text: def predicted_junctions(transcripts, locus): """Normalized decoded transcripts: chrom, strand, half-open exon intervals. Select by transcript-span overlap with the gene, then retain ALL introns. No strand-based overlap filter: wrong-strand predictions stay penalized. """ genes = w.genes_by_chromosome([locus]) result = set() for tx in transcripts: exons = sorted(tx['exons']) if (not exons or tx['strand'] not in ('+', '-') or any(type(a) is not int or type(z) is not int or not 0 <= a < z for a, z in exons) or any(a[1] >= z[0] for a, z in zip(exons, exons[1:]))): raise ValueError('invalid transcript exons/strand') if w.transcript_overlaps_gene(tx['chrom'], exons[0][0], exons[-1][1] - 1, genes): result.update((tx['chrom'], a[1], z[0] - 1, tx['strand']) for a, z in zip(exons, exons[1:])) return result

nodes.name: junction_counts
nodes.body_text: def junction_counts(predicted, supported, locus): """Predicted set already selected by transcript-overlaps-gene, not clipped.""" if supported is None: return None windows = w.windows_by_chromosome([locus]) supported = {j for j in supported if w.junction_within_windows(*j[:3], windows)} genes = w.genes_by_chromosome([locus]) recall = {j for j in supported if w.junction_within_genes(*j[:3], genes)} return dict(predicted=len(predicted), precision_tp=len(predicted & supported), supported=len(recall), recall_tp=len(predicted & recall))

nodes.name: metric
nodes.body_text: def metric(rows, fraction, name, seeds=(1, 2, 3)): counts = [r['seeds'][str(s)][fraction] for r in rows for s in seeds] total = lambda key: sum(c[key] for c in counts) if name == 'F1': denominator = total('f1_predicted') + total('f1_reference') return 200 * total('f1_tp') / denominator if denominator else float('nan') numerator, denominator = ('precision_tp', 'predicted') if name == 'P' else ('recall_tp', 'supported') d = total(denominator) return total(numerator) / d if d else float('nan')

nodes.name: score
nodes.body_text: def score(payload, panel): if set(payload['pairs']) != {'1', '2', '3'}: raise ValueError('exact seeds 1, 2, 3 required') paths = {s: Path(path).resolve(strict=True) for s, path in payload['pairs'].items()} seen = [] for path in paths.values(): if any(path == previous or path.samefile(previous) for previous in seen): raise ValueError('duplicate pair input file; seed labels do not establish run identity') seen.append(path) records = {int(s): [json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()] for s, path in paths.items()} rns, delta = b.build_tiles(records) primary = b.tile_bootstrap(delta) composite = math.fsum(r['composite_loss_off'] - r['composite_loss_on'] for rows in records.values() for r in rows if r['has_evidence']) / (3 * len(rns)) loci = payload['loci'] ids = [r['gene_id'] for r in loci] if len(ids) != len(set(ids)) or set(ids) != {l.gene_id for l in panel}: raise ValueError('exact full panel locus inventory required') loci = sorted(loci, key=lambda r: r['gene_id']) structural_flags = [] for row in loci: if set(row['seeds']) != {'1', '2', '3'}: raise ValueError('each locus must carry all three seeds') frozen = {} for pair in row['seeds'].values(): if set(pair) != {'off', 'on'}: raise ValueError('paired fractions off/on required') for c in pair.values(): required = {'f1_tp', 'f1_predicted', 'f1_reference'} structural = {'precision_tp', 'predicted', 'recall_tp', 'supported'} if set(c) not in (required, required | structural): raise ValueError('count schema mismatch') if any(type(v) is not int or v < 0 for v in c.values()): raise ValueError('counts must be nonnegative integers') if c['f1_tp'] > min(c['f1_predicted'], c['f1_reference']): raise ValueError('F1 numerator exceeds denominator') available = structural <= set(c) structural_flags.append(available) if available and (c['precision_tp'] > c['predicted'] or c['recall_tp'] > c['supported']): raise ValueError('junction numerator exceeds denominator') if available and c['recall_tp'] > c['precision_tp']: raise ValueError('recall true positives must be a subset of precision true positives') for field in ['f1_reference'] + (['supported'] if available else []): if c[field] != frozen.setdefault(field, c[field]): raise ValueError(f'{field} must be frozen across all fractions and seeds per locus') if any(structural_flags) != all(structural_flags): raise ValueError('partially missing structural scoring; do not encode missing as negative') result = dict(label='exploratory / MVP', panel_sha256=w.PANEL_SHA256, primary=primary, composite_delta_diagnostic=composite, structural_available=all(structural_flags), readouts={}, training_eligible=False, pair_run_provenance_status='UNVERIFIED', three_seed_identity_verified=False, three_seed_policy_verified=False, decision=None, decision_status='BLOCKED_PENDING_COVERAGE_POLICY', precision_rule='point_estimate_ge_0; interpretation pending author review') core = {l.gene_id for l in panel if l.panel == 'mvp_core'} for stratum, rows in [('all50', loci), ('core20', [r for r in loci if r['gene_id'] in core])]: result['readouts'][stratum] = {} for name in ['F1'] + (['P', 'R'] if all(structural_flags) else []): by_seed = {} for label, seeds in [('pooled', (1, 2, 3)), ('1', (1,)), ('2', (2,)), ('3', (3,))]: try: by_seed[label] = b.locus_bootstrap(rows, lambda sample: metric(sample, 'on', name, seeds) - metric(sample, 'off', name, seeds)) except b.BootstrapError as e: by_seed[label] = {'status': 'UNASSESSABLE', 'reason': str(e)} result['readouts'][stratum][name] = by_seed return result

nodes.body_text: def main(argv=None): p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__) p.add_argument('--input', required=True, type=Path) p.add_argument('--panels', required=True, type=Path) p.add_argument('--out', required=True, type=Path) p.add_argument('--final-decision', action='store_true', help='currently fail-closed pending author policy') a = p.parse_args(argv) if a.final_decision: require_coverage_policy(None) input_hash = w.sha256_file(a.input) payload = json.loads(a.input.read_text()) hashes = {str(path): w.sha256_file(path) for path in [a.panels, *payload['pairs'].values()]} hashes[str(a.input)] = input_hash result = score(payload, w.load_panel(a.panels)) if any(w.sha256_file(path) != expected for path, expected in hashes.items()): raise ValueError('scoring input changed during computation') result['input_sha256'] = hashes result['count_provenance_status'] = 'caller-supplied counts; not independently verified by this adapter' with a.out.open('x') as f: json.dump(result, f, indent=2, allow_nan=False) return 0

d.require(fa.read_text() == f'>{locus.gene_id} {locus.chromosome}:{start}-{end} genomic_forward
{sequence}
', 'panel sequence bytes mismatch') track = row['track'] d.require(track['dtype'] == 'float16' and track['shape'] == [30720,8], 'panel track metadata mismatch') array = np.load(artifact(track), allow_pickle=False) d.require(array.dtype == np.float16 and array.shape == (30720,8), 'panel track shape mismatch') d.require(np.isfinite(array).all() and (array >= 0).all(), 'invalid tracks') masked = np.frombuffer(sequence.upper().encode('ascii'), dtype='S1') == b'N' d.require(not array[masked].any() and (array[~masked,7] == 1).all(), 'N mask/availability mismatch') d.require((array[:,:3] <= np.float16(np.log1p(64))).all(), 'coverage cap exceeded') # Independently reproduce actual excluded-heldout selection and all three seeds. d.require(np.array_equal(array, p.panel_tracks(con, sequence, locus.chromosome, start)), 'panel rasterization mismatch') provenance = list(p.selected_provenance(con, locus.chromosome, start, end)) d.require(artifact(row['provenance']).read_text() == ''.join(p.canonical(r) for r in provenance), 'panel provenance mismatch') biological = np.count_nonzero(array[:,:7], axis=0).tolist() d.require(row['selected_molecule_count'] == len(provenance) and row['biological_nonzero_per_channel'] == biological and row['availability_nonzero'] == int(np.count_nonzero(array[:,7])) and row['zero_biological_support'] is (not any(biological)), 'panel support summary mismatch') result[locus.gene_id] = torch.from_numpy(array.copy()).unsqueeze(0) p.unchanged(records) return result, records

nodes.name: artifact
nodes.body_text: def artifact(record): relative = Path(record['path']) path = root / relative d.require(not relative.is_absolute() and '..' not in relative.parts and path.resolve(strict=True).is_relative_to(root), 'panel artifact path escape') d.require(path.resolve() == path.absolute(), 'panel artifact symlink is not permitted') d.require(str(relative) not in paths, 'duplicate panel artifact') paths.add(str(relative)) actual = d.checked_file(dict(path=str(path), sha256=record['sha256'], size=record['bytes'])) records.append(actual) return path

nodes.name: test_as_addition_scoring.py
nodes.body_text: """Tests for 34_score_as_additions.py. Every test here is written against a behaviour that could plausibly go wrong in the direction that flatters the result, because that is how this benchmark has failed before: a quantity that counted one side of a ledger and never the other. So the suite checks the gain side as well as the loss side — additions that should NOT be counted, denominators that should NOT silently shrink, and matches that should NOT be credited. """ import importlib.util import json import sys from pathlib import Path import pytest spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location( "as_additions", Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "34_score_as_additions.py") mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) sys.modules["as_additions"] = mod spec.loader.exec_module(mod) # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- fixtures PRIMARY = [(100, 200), (300, 400)] ALT1 = [(100, 200), (320, 400)] ALT2 = [(100, 200), (340, 400)] @pytest.fixture # ------------------------------------------------------------------ the headline counts # ------------------------------------------------------------------- the intron chain # ------------------------------------------------------------------------ AtRTD3 side # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- the pairing # --------------------------------------------------------- denominators and gain side # ---------------------------------------------------------------- reference resolution # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- CLI # ------------------------------------- TAIR10's primary, scored apart from its alternatives # A structure that is neither TAIR10's primary nor either of its alternatives. Used as the # prompt so that an addition CAN equal the primary — when the prompt already is the # primary, an emission of it is excluded as "equal to the prompt" and never reaches this # code path at all. TOOL_ONLY = [(100, 200), (360, 400)] # ------------------------- the subset where the prompt was already a real TAIR10 transcript

nodes.name: _gff3
nodes.signature: def _gff3(path: Path, loci: list[dict], extra_lines: list[str] | None = None) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _gff3(path: Path, loci: list[dict], extra_lines: list[str] | None = None) -> None: """Write a real 3-level gene -> mRNA -> CDS GFF3. Each locus dict takes: gene gene id, written as ID= on the gene row seq sequence name (default "Chr1") strand (default "+") name when given, written as Name= BEFORE ID= — GeMoMa's attribute order, which is what makes the model's GM= value the Name and not the ID gm when given, written as GM= on every row, as completion-mode output does transcripts [(transcript_id, [(start, end), ...]), ...] in file order; the FIRST one is what preprocess.py hands the decoder as the prompt """ lines: list[str] = [] for locus in loci: seq = locus.get("seq", "Chr1") strand = locus.get("strand", "+") segments = [s for _tx, segs in locus["transcripts"] for s in segs] gene_start = min(s for s, _e in segments) gene_end = max(e for _s, e in segments) attrs: list[str] = [] if locus.get("name"): attrs.append(f"Name={locus['name']}") attrs.append(f"ID={locus['gene']}") gm = f";GM={locus['gm']}" if locus.get("gm") else "" lines.append(f"{seq}\tsrc\tgene\t{gene_start}\t{gene_end}\t.\t{strand}\t.\t" + ";".join(attrs) + gm) for tx, segs in locus["transcripts"]: lines.append(f"{seq}\tsrc\tmRNA\t{min(s for s, _e in segs)}\t" f"{max(e for _s, e in segs)}\t.\t{strand}\t.\t" f"ID={tx};Parent={locus['gene']}{gm}") for n, (s, e) in enumerate(segs, 1): lines.append(f"{seq}\tsrc\tCDS\t{s}\t{e}\t.\t{strand}\t0\t" f"ID={tx}.cds{n};Parent={tx}{gm}") lines.extend(extra_lines or []) path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")

nodes.name: _gtf
nodes.body_text: def _gtf(path: Path, loci: list[dict]) -> None: """Write a TAIR10/AtRTD3-shaped GTF (transcript/exon/CDS rows, gene_id + transcript_id).""" lines: list[str] = [] for locus in loci: seq = locus.get("seq", "Chr1") strand = locus.get("strand", "+") for tx, segs in locus["transcripts"]: attr = f'transcript_id "{tx}"; gene_id "{locus["gene"]}";' lines.append(f"{seq}\tsrc\ttranscript\t{min(s for s, _e in segs)}\t" f"{max(e for _s, e in segs)}\t.\t{strand}\t.\t{attr}") for s, e in segs: lines.append(f"{seq}\tsrc\texon\t{s}\t{e}\t.\t{strand}\t.\t{attr}") lines.append(f"{seq}\tsrc\tCDS\t{s}\t{e}\t.\t{strand}\t0\t{attr}") path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")

nodes.name: refs
nodes.body_text: def refs(tmp_path): """A one-locus TAIR10 with one primary and two alternatives, plus an empty AtRTD3.""" tair10 = tmp_path / "tair10.gtf" atrtd3 = tmp_path / "atrtd3.gtf" primary_ids = tmp_path / "primary.txt" _gtf(tair10, [{"gene": "AT1G01010", "transcripts": [("AT1G01010.1", PRIMARY), ("AT1G01010.2", ALT1), ("AT1G01010.3", ALT2)]}]) _gtf(atrtd3, [{"gene": "AT9G99999", "seq": "Chr9", "transcripts": [("AT9G99999.1", [(10, 20)])]}]) primary_ids.write_text("AT1G01010.1\n") return dict(tair10=tair10, atrtd3=atrtd3, primary_ids=primary_ids)

nodes.name: _score
nodes.body_text: def _score(tmp_path, refs, input_loci, output_loci, extra_input_lines=None): inp = tmp_path / "in.gff3" out = tmp_path / "out.gff3" _gff3(inp, input_loci, extra_input_lines) _gff3(out, output_loci) return mod.score(inp, out, refs["tair10"], refs["atrtd3"], refs["primary_ids"])

Both definitions are reported: `added_structures` counts everything that differs from the prompt (what the model was actually given), the decomposition field counts only what differs from every transcript the input already held (32_score_polishing.py's definition). They coincide exactly when the input is single-transcript per locus. """ r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("G1.t1", PRIMARY), ("G1.t2", ALT1)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("O1.t1", PRIMARY), ("O1.t2", ALT1), ("O1.t3", ALT2)]}]) assert r["added_structures"] == 2 assert r["decomposition"]["added_structures_vs_all_input_transcripts"] == 1 assert r["decomposition"]["input_loci_with_multiple_transcripts"] == 1 assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_exact_CDS"] == 2

nodes.body_text: def test_intron_chain_match_is_looser_than_exact_cds(tmp_path, refs): terminus_variant = [(90, 200), (320, 410)] # ALT1's chain, different termini r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("G1.t1", PRIMARY)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("O1.t1", PRIMARY), ("O1.t2", terminus_variant)]}]) assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_exact_CDS"] == 0 assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_intron_chain"] == 1 assert r["precision_vs_TAIR10_alternatives_intron_chain_pct"] == 100.0

nodes.body_text: def test_chain_match_that_reuses_the_prompt_chain_is_reported_separately(tmp_path, refs): """The 48x swing between exact-CDS and intron-chain precision recorded in 32_score_polishing.py's docstring was almost entirely terminus variants of the supplied transcript. That decomposition has to be visible, not inferable.""" prompt_chain_variant = [(90, 200), (300, 410)] # PRIMARY's chain, different termini ref = tmp_path / "ref.gtf" _gtf(ref, [{"gene": "AT1G01010", "transcripts": [("AT1G01010.1", PRIMARY), ("AT1G01010.2", [(95, 200), (300, 405)])]}]) inp, out = tmp_path / "in.gff3", tmp_path / "out.gff3" _gff3(inp, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("G1.t1", PRIMARY)]}]) _gff3(out, [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("O1.t1", PRIMARY), ("O1.t2", prompt_chain_variant)]}]) r = mod.score(inp, out, ref, refs["atrtd3"], refs["primary_ids"]) d = r["decomposition"] assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_intron_chain"] == 1 assert d["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_intron_chain_reusing_prompt_chain"] == 1 assert d["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_intron_chain_distinct_from_prompt"] == 0

nodes.name: test_tair10_gene_id_suffix_is_normalised_before_joining_to_atrtd3
nodes.body_text: def test_tair10_gene_id_suffix_is_normalised_before_joining_to_atrtd3(tmp_path): """TAIR10.gtf writes gene_id "AT1G01010.TAIR10"; AtRTD3 writes "AT1G01010". Without normalisation every AtRTD3 lookup misses and the count is a silent, plausible 0.""" tair10, atrtd3, primary_ids = (tmp_path / "t.gtf", tmp_path / "a.gtf", tmp_path / "p.txt") _gtf(tair10, [{"gene": "AT1G01010.TAIR10", "transcripts": [("AT1G01010.1.TAIR10", PRIMARY), ("AT1G01010.2.TAIR10", ALT1)]}]) _gtf(atrtd3, [{"gene": "AT1G01010", "transcripts": [("AT1G01010.1", PRIMARY), ("AT1G01010.2", ALT1)]}]) primary_ids.write_text("AT1G01010.1.TAIR10\n") inp, out = tmp_path / "in.gff3", tmp_path / "out.gff3" _gff3(inp, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("G1.t1", PRIMARY)]}]) _gff3(out, [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("O1.t1", PRIMARY), ("O1.t2", ALT1)]}]) r = mod.score(inp, out, tair10, atrtd3, primary_ids) assert r["added_matching_any_AtRTD3_transcript"] == 1 assert r["diagnostics"]["reference_loci_without_AtRTD3_counterpart"] == 0

nodes.name: test_gm_pairs_on_the_first_attribute_value_not_the_id
nodes.body_text: def test_gm_pairs_on_the_first_attribute_value_not_the_id(tmp_path, refs): """GeMoMa's gene rows lead with Name=, and preprocess.py derives GM= from whichever attribute comes first. Matching GM= against ID= silently sends every locus down the positional fallback — measured on the real GeMoMa run as gm_paired=0 of 29,561.""" r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "gene_0", "name": "Ath_00001", "transcripts": [("gene_0.t1", PRIMARY)]}], [{"gene": "A_thaliana_g000001", "gm": "Ath_00001", "transcripts": [("A_thaliana_g000001.t1", PRIMARY), ("A_thaliana_g000001.t2", ALT1)]}]) assert r["diagnostics"]["pairing"]["gm_paired"] == 1 assert r["diagnostics"]["pairing"]["overlap_fallback"] == 0 assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_exact_CDS"] == 1

nodes.name: test_gene_ids_are_never_compared_across_files
nodes.body_text: def test_gene_ids_are_never_compared_across_files(tmp_path, refs): """standardize_gff.py renumbers by sort position, so the output's ID=A_thaliana_g000001 is a DIFFERENT locus from the input's ID=A_thaliana_g000001 whenever anything upstream was dropped. Pairing must follow GM=, which carries the real provenance.""" far = [(1000, 1100), (1300, 1400)] far_alt = [(1000, 1100), (1320, 1400)] tair10 = tmp_path / "t.gtf" _gtf(tair10, [{"gene": "AT1G01010", "transcripts": [("AT1G01010.1", PRIMARY), ("AT1G01010.2", ALT1)]}, {"gene": "AT1G01020", "transcripts": [("AT1G01020.1", far), ("AT1G01020.2", far_alt)]}]) inp, out = tmp_path / "in.gff3", tmp_path / "out.gff3" _gff3(inp, [{"gene": "A_thaliana_g000001", "transcripts": [("t1", PRIMARY)]}, {"gene": "A_thaliana_g000002", "transcripts": [("t2", far)]}]) _gff3(out, [{"gene": "A_thaliana_g000001", "gm": "A_thaliana_g000002", "transcripts": [("o1", far), ("o2", far_alt)]}]) r = mod.score(inp, out, tair10, refs["atrtd3"], refs["primary_ids"]) assert r["diagnostics"]["pairing"]["gm_paired"] == 1 assert r["loci_scored"] == 1 assert r["diagnostics"]["loci_without_output"] == 1 assert r["added_structures"] == 1 assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_exact_CDS"] == 1

nodes.name: test_ambiguous_first_attribute_values_are_reported_not_guessed
nodes.body_text: def test_ambiguous_first_attribute_values_are_reported_not_guessed(tmp_path, refs): """Two input genes sharing a Name= would make GM= ambiguous. Picking one at random would be a silent mis-attribution; those loci must fall to the positional fallback and the ambiguity must appear in the JSON.""" far = [(1000, 1100), (1300, 1400)] r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "gene_0", "name": "dup", "transcripts": [("a", PRIMARY)]}, {"gene": "gene_1", "name": "dup", "transcripts": [("b", far)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "dup", "transcripts": [("o1", PRIMARY), ("o2", ALT1)]}]) assert r["diagnostics"]["ambiguous_input_gm_keys"] == 2 assert r["diagnostics"]["pairing"]["gm_paired"] == 0 assert r["diagnostics"]["pairing"]["overlap_fallback"] == 1

nodes.name: test_locus_without_output_is_excluded_from_the_denominator_and_reported
nodes.body_text: def test_locus_without_output_is_excluded_from_the_denominator_and_reported(tmp_path, refs): far = [(1000, 1100), (1300, 1400)] far_alt = [(1000, 1100), (1320, 1400)] tair10 = tmp_path / "t.gtf" _gtf(tair10, [{"gene": "AT1G01010", "transcripts": [("AT1G01010.1", PRIMARY), ("AT1G01010.2", ALT1)]}, {"gene": "AT1G01020", "transcripts": [("AT1G01020.1", far), ("AT1G01020.2", far_alt)]}]) inp, out = tmp_path / "in.gff3", tmp_path / "out.gff3" _gff3(inp, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("t1", PRIMARY)]}, {"gene": "G2", "transcripts": [("t2", far)]}]) _gff3(out, [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("o1", PRIMARY), ("o2", ALT1)]}]) r = mod.score(inp, out, tair10, refs["atrtd3"], refs["primary_ids"]) assert r["loci_scored"] == 1 assert r["diagnostics"]["loci_without_output"] == 1 # G2's alternative is not recoverable and must not dilute recall — but it must not # vanish either, or a reader cannot tell coverage from performance. assert r["reference_alternative_transcripts"] == 1 assert r["diagnostics"]["reference_alternative_transcripts_at_loci_without_output"] == 1 assert r["recall_of_TAIR10_alternatives_pct"] == 100.0

nodes.name: test_output_locus_with_no_input_partner_is_counted
nodes.body_text: def test_output_locus_with_no_input_partner_is_counted(tmp_path, refs): """The excess/gain side. Every previous defect in this benchmark counted loss and never gain; an output locus that corresponds to no input locus is exactly that.""" r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("t1", PRIMARY)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("o1", PRIMARY), ("o2", ALT1)]}, {"gene": "O2", "gm": "ghost", "seq": "Chr2", "transcripts": [("o3", [(5000, 5100), (5300, 5400)])]}]) assert r["diagnostics"]["output_loci"] == 2 assert r["diagnostics"]["output_loci_without_input_partner"] == 1

nodes.name: test_prompt_survival_splits_additions_from_replacements
nodes.body_text: def test_prompt_survival_splits_additions_from_replacements(tmp_path, refs): """An "addition" at a locus whose prompt was destroyed is a replacement, not an added isoform. 84-89% of `added_structures` sat there in the polishing run.""" far = [(1000, 1100), (1300, 1400)] far_alt = [(1000, 1100), (1320, 1400)] tair10 = tmp_path / "t.gtf" _gtf(tair10, [{"gene": "AT1G01010", "transcripts": [("AT1G01010.1", PRIMARY), ("AT1G01010.2", ALT1)]}, {"gene": "AT1G01020", "transcripts": [("AT1G01020.1", far), ("AT1G01020.2", far_alt)]}]) inp, out = tmp_path / "in.gff3", tmp_path / "out.gff3" _gff3(inp, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("t1", PRIMARY)]}, {"gene": "G2", "transcripts": [("t2", far)]}]) _gff3(out, [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("o1", PRIMARY), ("o2", ALT1)]}, {"gene": "O2", "gm": "G2", "transcripts": [("o3", far_alt)]}]) r = mod.score(inp, out, tair10, refs["atrtd3"], refs["primary_ids"]) d = r["decomposition"] assert r["added_structures"] == 2 assert d["prompt_survived_loci"] == 1 assert d["prompt_destroyed_loci"] == 1 assert d["added_at_loci_where_prompt_survived"] == 1 assert d["added_at_loci_where_prompt_destroyed"] == 1 assert d["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_exact_CDS_at_prompt_survived_loci"] == 1

nodes.name: test_additions_at_loci_with_no_reference_gene_are_disclosed
nodes.body_text: def test_additions_at_loci_with_no_reference_gene_are_disclosed(tmp_path, refs): """They cannot be right against TAIR10 and are kept in the headline denominator (the same convention 28_score_added_isoforms.py uses), so the restricted denominator has to be reported alongside or the precision floor reads as a measurement.""" orphan = [(9000, 9100), (9300, 9400)] orphan_alt = [(9000, 9100), (9320, 9400)] r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("t1", PRIMARY)]}, {"gene": "G2", "seq": "Chr8", "transcripts": [("t2", orphan)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("o1", PRIMARY), ("o2", ALT1)]}, {"gene": "O2", "gm": "G2", "seq": "Chr8", "transcripts": [("o3", orphan), ("o4", orphan_alt)]}]) d = r["decomposition"] assert r["added_structures"] == 2 assert d["added_structures_at_reference_matched_loci"] == 1 assert r["precision_vs_TAIR10_alternatives_pct"] == 50.0 assert d["precision_vs_TAIR10_alternatives_at_reference_matched_loci_pct"] == 100.0 assert r["diagnostics"]["input_loci_without_reference_match"] == 1

nodes.name: test_the_field_that_reconciles_with_32_score_polishing_is_reported
nodes.body_text: def test_the_field_that_reconciles_with_32_score_polishing_is_reported(tmp_path, refs): """`32_score_polishing.py.added_structures` differs from this module's headline on two axes at once — it counts only at reference-matched loci, and only structures absent from the whole input locus. Both restrictions applied together is the one field that has to reproduce it, so all four combinations are asserted here.""" orphan = [(9000, 9100), (9300, 9400)] orphan_alt = [(9000, 9100), (9320, 9400)] r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("t1", PRIMARY), ("t2", ALT1)]}, {"gene": "G2", "seq": "Chr8", "transcripts": [("t3", orphan)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("o1", PRIMARY), ("o2", ALT1), ("o3", ALT2)]}, {"gene": "O2", "gm": "G2", "seq": "Chr8", "transcripts": [("o4", orphan), ("o5", orphan_alt)]}]) d = r["decomposition"] assert r["added_structures"] == 3 # prompt, all loci assert d["added_structures_vs_all_input_transcripts"] == 2 # all-input, all loci assert d["added_structures_at_reference_matched_loci"] == 2 # prompt, matched assert d["added_structures_vs_all_input_transcripts_at_reference_matched_loci"] == 1

nodes.name: test_reference_primary_comes_from_primary_ids_not_file_order
nodes.body_text: def test_reference_primary_comes_from_primary_ids_not_file_order(tmp_path, refs): """If file order picked the primary here, ALT1 would be treated as the primary and excluded from the alternatives, and a correct addition would score as wrong.""" tair10 = tmp_path / "t.gtf" _gtf(tair10, [{"gene": "AT1G01010", "transcripts": [("AT1G01010.2", ALT1), # alternative, written FIRST ("AT1G01010.1", PRIMARY)]}]) inp, out = tmp_path / "in.gff3", tmp_path / "out.gff3" _gff3(inp, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("t1", PRIMARY)]}]) _gff3(out, [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("o1", PRIMARY), ("o2", ALT1)]}]) r = mod.score(inp, out, tair10, refs["atrtd3"], refs["primary_ids"]) assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_exact_CDS"] == 1 assert r["diagnostics"]["reference_primary_fallback_to_file_order"] == 0

nodes.name: test_exact_match_on_the_opposite_strand_is_flagged
nodes.body_text: def test_exact_match_on_the_opposite_strand_is_flagged(tmp_path, refs): """CDS structures are compared as coordinate tuples, so an antisense overlapping gene can produce a coordinate-identical "match" that is biologically nothing.""" tair10 = tmp_path / "t.gtf" _gtf(tair10, [{"gene": "AT1G01010", "strand": "-", "transcripts": [("AT1G01010.1", PRIMARY), ("AT1G01010.2", ALT1)]}]) inp, out = tmp_path / "in.gff3", tmp_path / "out.gff3" _gff3(inp, [{"gene": "G1", "strand": "+", "transcripts": [("t1", PRIMARY)]}]) _gff3(out, [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "strand": "+", "transcripts": [("o1", PRIMARY), ("o2", ALT1)]}]) r = mod.score(inp, out, tair10, refs["atrtd3"], refs["primary_ids"]) assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_exact_CDS"] == 1 assert r["diagnostics"][ "added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_exact_CDS_opposite_strand"] == 1

nodes.name: test_noncoding_input_features_are_excluded_and_reported
nodes.body_text: def test_noncoding_input_features_are_excluded_and_reported(tmp_path, refs): lnc = ["Chr1\tsrc\tlnc_RNA\t2000\t2100\t.\t+\t.\tID=nc1", "Chr1\tsrc\texon\t2000\t2100\t.\t+\t.\tID=nc1.e1;Parent=nc1"] r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("t1", PRIMARY)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("o1", PRIMARY), ("o2", ALT1)]}], extra_input_lines=lnc) assert r["diagnostics"]["input_noncoding_features_excluded"] == {"lnc_RNA": 1} assert r["diagnostics"]["input_coding_loci"] == 1

nodes.name: test_cli_records_every_argument_in_provenance
nodes.body_text: def test_cli_records_every_argument_in_provenance(tmp_path, refs): inp, out, js = tmp_path / "in.gff3", tmp_path / "out.gff3", tmp_path / "r.json" _gff3(inp, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("t1", PRIMARY)]}]) _gff3(out, [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("o1", PRIMARY), ("o2", ALT1)]}]) rc = mod.main(["--input", str(inp), "--output", str(out), "--tool", "helixer", "--tair10", str(refs["tair10"]), "--atrtd3", str(refs["atrtd3"]), "--primary-ids", str(refs["primary_ids"]), "--json", str(js)]) assert rc == 0 p = json.loads(js.read_text())["provenance"] assert p["tool"] == "helixer" assert p["input"] == str(inp) assert p["output"] == str(out) assert p["reference_TAIR10"] == str(refs["tair10"]) assert p["reference_AtRTD3"] == str(refs["atrtd3"]) assert p["primary_ids"] == str(refs["primary_ids"]) for key in ("input", "output", "tool", "tair10", "atrtd3", "primary_ids", "json"): assert key in p["cli_args"] assert p["argv"][0] == "--input"

nodes.name: test_empty_side_raises_rather_than_reporting_zeros
nodes.body_text: def test_empty_side_raises_rather_than_reporting_zeros(tmp_path, refs): inp, out = tmp_path / "in.gff3", tmp_path / "out.gff3" _gff3(inp, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("t1", PRIMARY)]}]) out.write_text("##gff-version 3\n") with pytest.raises(ValueError): mod.score(inp, out, refs["tair10"], refs["atrtd3"], refs["primary_ids"])

nodes.name: test_addition_equal_to_the_tair10_primary_is_counted_as_primary_not_alternative
nodes.body_text: def test_addition_equal_to_the_tair10_primary_is_counted_as_primary_not_alternative( tmp_path, refs): r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("G1.t1", TOOL_ONLY)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("O1.t1", TOOL_ONLY), ("O1.t2", PRIMARY)]}]) assert r["added_structures"] == 1 assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_primary"] == 1 # It must NOT leak into the alternatives headline the manuscript's 18.1% compares to. assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_exact_CDS"] == 0 assert r["precision_vs_TAIR10_alternatives_pct"] == 0.0 assert r["precision_vs_TAIR10_primary_pct"] == 100.0

nodes.body_text: def test_any_transcript_is_the_union_of_primary_and_alternative_hits(tmp_path, refs): r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("G1.t1", TOOL_ONLY)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("O1.t1", TOOL_ONLY), ("O1.t2", PRIMARY), ("O1.t3", ALT1)]}]) assert r["added_structures"] == 2 assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_primary"] == 1 assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_exact_CDS"] == 1 assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_any_transcript"] == 2 assert r["precision_vs_TAIR10_any_transcript_pct"] == 100.0

nodes.body_text: def test_primary_hit_is_zero_when_only_alternatives_are_added(tmp_path, refs): r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("G1.t1", PRIMARY)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("O1.t1", PRIMARY), ("O1.t2", ALT1)]}]) assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_primary"] == 0 assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_any_transcript"] == 1 assert r["precision_vs_TAIR10_primary_pct"] == 0.0

nodes.name: test_re_emitting_the_prompt_never_counts_as_a_primary_hit
nodes.body_text: def test_re_emitting_the_prompt_never_counts_as_a_primary_hit(tmp_path, refs): """The prompt IS TAIR10's primary here; re-emitting it is not an addition at all.""" r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("G1.t1", PRIMARY)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("O1.t1", PRIMARY)]}]) assert r["added_structures"] == 0 assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_primary"] == 0 assert r["precision_vs_TAIR10_primary_pct"] is None

nodes.body_text: def test_primary_hit_that_replaced_the_prompt_is_not_attributed_to_survival(tmp_path, refs): """The prompt is gone and TAIR10's primary stands in its place — a replacement.""" r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("G1.t1", TOOL_ONLY)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("O1.t1", PRIMARY)]}]) assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_primary"] == 1 assert r["decomposition"]["prompt_destroyed_loci"] == 1 assert r["decomposition"]["added_matching_TAIR10_primary_at_prompt_survived_loci"] == 0

nodes.body_text: def test_locus_whose_prompt_equals_a_reference_transcript_is_isolated(tmp_path, refs): r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("G1.t1", PRIMARY)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("O1.t1", PRIMARY), ("O1.t2", ALT1)]}]) d = r["decomposition"] assert d["loci_where_prompt_equals_a_reference_transcript"] == 1 assert d["added_at_loci_where_prompt_is_correct"] == 1 assert d["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_at_loci_where_prompt_is_correct"] == 1 assert d["precision_vs_TAIR10_alternatives_at_loci_where_prompt_is_correct_pct"] == 100.0

nodes.name: test_a_prompt_matching_an_alternative_also_counts_as_correct
nodes.body_text: def test_a_prompt_matching_an_alternative_also_counts_as_correct(tmp_path, refs): """"Correct" means it equals ANY TAIR10 transcript, not specifically the primary.""" r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("G1.t1", ALT1)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("O1.t1", ALT1), ("O1.t2", ALT2)]}]) d = r["decomposition"] assert d["loci_where_prompt_equals_a_reference_transcript"] == 1 assert d["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_at_loci_where_prompt_is_correct"] == 1

nodes.name: test_locus_with_a_wrong_prompt_is_excluded_from_the_subset
nodes.body_text: def test_locus_with_a_wrong_prompt_is_excluded_from_the_subset(tmp_path, refs): r = _score(tmp_path, refs, [{"gene": "G1", "transcripts": [("G1.t1", TOOL_ONLY)]}], [{"gene": "O1", "gm": "G1", "transcripts": [("O1.t1", TOOL_ONLY), ("O1.t2", ALT1)]}]) d = r["decomposition"] assert d["loci_where_prompt_equals_a_reference_transcript"] == 0 assert d["added_at_loci_where_prompt_is_correct"] == 0 # N/A rather than 0.0 — nothing was measured on an empty subset. assert d["precision_vs_TAIR10_alternatives_at_loci_where_prompt_is_correct_pct"] is None # ...while the headline still counts the addition. assert r["added_matching_TAIR10_alternative_exact_CDS"] == 1

nodes.name: test_b6_panels.py
nodes.body_text: """B6 locus panels (A46): eligibility helpers of 71_b6_panels.py, panel assignment of 72_mvp_select_loci.py and the samtools helper 72a_est_molecules_per_locus.sh.""" import importlib.util import shutil import subprocess import sys from pathlib import Path import pytest SCRIPTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] panels71 = load("panels71", "71_b6_panels.py") select72 = load("select72", "72_mvp_select_loci.py") GFF = """\ Chr1\tsrc\tgene\t101\t400\t.\t+\t.\tID=G1;Name=G1 Chr1\tsrc\tmRNA\t101\t400\t.\t+\t.\tID=G1.1;Parent=G1 Chr1\tsrc\texon\t101\t150\t.\t+\t.\tID=e1;Parent=G1.1 Chr1\tsrc\texon\t200\t250\t.\t+\t.\tID=e2;Parent=G1.1 Chr1\tsrc\texon\t300\t400\t.\t+\t.\tID=e3;Parent=G1.1 Chr1\tsrc\tmRNA\t101\t400\t.\t+\t.\tID=G1.2;Parent=G1 Chr1\tsrc\texon\t101\t150\t.\t+\t.\tID=e4;Parent=G1.2 Chr1\tsrc\texon\t300\t400\t.\t+\t.\tID=e5;Parent=G1.2 Chr1\tsrc\tgene\t501\t600\t.\t-\t.\tID=G2 Chr1\tsrc\tmRNA\t501\t600\t.\t-\t.\tID=G2.1;Parent=G2 Chr1\tsrc\tCDS\t501\t600\t.\t-\t0\tID=c1;Parent=G2.1 """ @pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("samtools") is None, reason="samtools not installed")

nodes.name: load
nodes.body_text: def load(name, filename): spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, SCRIPTS / filename) mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) spec.loader.exec_module(mod) return mod

nodes.body_text: def test_parse_gff_counts_max_exons_per_transcript_and_cds_fallback(tmp_path): gff = tmp_path / "g.gff3" gff.write_text(GFF) genes = panels71.parse_gff_genes(gff) assert genes["G1"] == {"chrom": "Chr1", "start0": 100, "end0": 400, "strand": "+", "n_transcripts": 2, "exon_count": 3} assert genes["G2"]["exon_count"] == 1 and genes["G2"]["n_transcripts"] == 1 and genes["G2"]["strand"] == "-"

nodes.body_text: def test_overlapping_genes_marks_both_partners_on_either_strand(): # (gene_id, gene_id_original, chromosome, start0, end0, ...) genes = [("A", "a", "Chr1", 0, 100), ("B", "b", "Chr1", 99, 200), ("C", "c", "Chr1", 200, 300), ("D", "d", "Chr2", 0, 100)] assert panels71.overlapping_genes(genes, 0) == {"A", "B"} # half-open: C touches B without overlap assert panels71.overlapping_genes(genes, 1) == {"A", "B", "C"} # a 1-nt flank makes B and C overlap

nodes.name: make_pool
nodes.body_text: def make_pool(n, long_ranks=()): rows = [] for i in range(1, n + 1): length = 25000 if i in long_ranks else 1000 + i rows.append({"shuffle_rank": i, "species_id": "Athaliana", "gene_id": f"Ath{i:06d}", "chromosome": "Chr1", "start": 10000 * i, "fin": 10000 * i + length - 1, "strand": "+", "length": length, "orthogroup_id": "" if i % 7 == 0 else f"HOG{i}", "n_transcripts": 1, "exon_count": 3, "intron_count": 2}) return rows

nodes.name: test_select_panels_walks_rank_order_and_applies_sub_filter
nodes.body_text: def test_select_panels_walks_rank_order_and_applies_sub_filter(): pool = make_pool(30, long_ranks=(2,)) counts = {r["gene_id"]: (1 if r["shuffle_rank"] == 4 else 5) for r in pool} report = [] rows = select72.select_panels(pool, counts, mvp=6, core=2, pilot=10, max_len=20000, min_est=3, report=report) by_rank = {r["shuffle_rank"]: r for r in rows} assert [r["shuffle_rank"] for r in rows if r["panel"] == "mvp_core"] == [1, 3] # rank 2 too long assert [r["shuffle_rank"] for r in rows if r["panel"] == "mvp"] == [5, 6, 7, 8] # rank 4 too few ESTs assert [r["shuffle_rank"] for r in rows if r["panel"] == "pilot"] == [2, 4] + list(range(9, 17)) assert all(r["panel"] == "final" for r in rows if r["shuffle_rank"] > 16) assert by_rank[1]["est_molecules"] == 5 and by_rank[2]["est_molecules"] == "" and by_rank[9]["est_molecules"] == "" assert [r["shuffle_rank"] for r in rows] == list(range(1, 31)) assert "panel_counts=" in report[-1] and '"mvp_core": 2' in report[-1] and '"pilot": 10' in report[-1]

nodes.name: test_select_panels_errors_when_walked_locus_has_no_count_or_pool_exhausted
nodes.body_text: def test_select_panels_errors_when_walked_locus_has_no_count_or_pool_exhausted(): pool = make_pool(5) with pytest.raises(select72.SelectError, match="no entry"): select72.select_panels(pool, {}, 2, 1, 1, 20000, 3, []) with pytest.raises(select72.SelectError, match="pool exhausted"): select72.select_panels(pool, {r["gene_id"]: 0 for r in pool}, 2, 1, 1, 20000, 3, [])

nodes.name: test_est_arm_report.py
nodes.body_text: """A37 paired reporting (66_est_arm_report.py). The parsing here is small but easy to get wrong in a way that would silently change a reported mapping rate: samtools writes the percentage inside the same line it writes the count, newer versions add a separate "primary mapped (" line that must not be mistaken for it, and supplementary records have to leave both numerator and denominator or the two arms stop being comparable to the 2026-09-03 table. """ import sys import types from pathlib import Path import pytest SCRIPT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "66_est_arm_report.py" mod = types.ModuleType("est_arm_report"); mod.__file__ = str(SCRIPT) sys.modules["est_arm_report"] = mod exec(compile(SCRIPT.read_text(), str(SCRIPT), "exec"), mod.__dict__) # samtools 1.3.1, the version the alignment actually runs (Athaliana primary, job 6148523_0) FLAGSTAT_1_3 = """1050677 + 0 in total (QC-passed reads + QC-failed reads) 0 + 0 secondary 3852 + 0 supplementary 0 + 0 duplicates 978663 + 0 mapped (93.15% : N/A) 0 + 0 paired in sequencing """ # A newer samtools adds "primary mapped"; it must not be read as the mapped count. FLAGSTAT_NEWER = """1050677 + 0 in total (QC-passed reads + QC-failed reads) 0 + 0 secondary 3852 + 0 supplementary 0 + 0 duplicates 978663 + 0 mapped (93.15% : N/A) 1046825 + 0 primary 974811 + 0 primary mapped (93.12% : N/A) """

nodes.body_text: def sam(name="read1", start=51, cigar="50M100N50M100N50M", cs=":50~gt100ag:50~gt100ag:50", flag=0, ts="+", mapq=60, extra=""): tags = f"cs:Z:{cs}\tAS:i:150" + (f"\tts:A:{ts}" if ts is not None else "") return f"{name}\t{flag}\tchr1\t{start}\t{mapq}\t{cigar}\t*\t0\t0\t*\t*\t{tags}{extra}\n"

nodes.name: addition
nodes.body_text: def addition(**kwargs): base = dict(addition_id="add1", locus_id="gene1", species="synthetic", assembly="fixture", contig="chr1", strand="+", cds_start=51, cds_end=400, locus_start=1, locus_end=500, introns=((101, 200), (251, 350)), novel_introns=((251, 350),), novelty="junction-novel", filter_pass=True, exact_cds_match=False) base.update(kwargs) return m.Addition(**base)

nodes.name: obs
nodes.signature: def obs(name="read1", source="ONT", library="lib", run="run1", g=None, **kwargs)
nodes.body_text: def obs(name="read1", source="ONT", library="lib", run="run1", g=None, **kwargs): a = m.parse_sam(sam(name=name, **kwargs)) strand = m.transcript_strand(a) return m.Observation(a, "synthetic", "fixture", source, "dataset", run, library, "project", "reference", "independent", True, strand, m.call_junctions(a, g or genome(), strand, source), metadata={ "protocol": "direct_RNA", "umi_status": "absent", "arm": "primary", "source_molecule": name})

nodes.name: score
nodes.body_text: def score(a, observations): return m.score_addition(a, m.assign_molecules(observations))

nodes.name: test_positive_complete_chain_control

nodes.body_text: def test_partial_control_does_not_assemble_a_combination(): left = [obs(f"l{i}", cigar="50M100N30M", cs=":50~gt100ag:30") for i in range(3)] right = [obs(f"r{i}", start=221, cigar="30M100N50M", cs=":30~gt100ag:50") for i in range(3)] a = addition(novelty="combination-novel", novel_introns=()) row = score(a, left + right) assert row["chain_support_single_read"] == "partial" assert row["constituent_junction_support"] is True assert row["chain_witness_reads"] == 0 and not row["chain_callable"] assert row["novel_junction_support"] == "N/A" and row["chain_reading_report"]["chain_support_single_read"]["tier"] == "T4" assert row["chain_reading_report"]["chain_support_single_read"]["chain_negative"] is None

nodes.name: test_ont_anchor_boundaries
nodes.signature: def test_ont_anchor_boundaries(cs, accepted): # Build matching CIGAR from cs so tests exercise junction filtering, not malformed input.
nodes.body_text: def test_ont_anchor_boundaries(cs, accepted): # Build matching CIGAR from cs so tests exercise junction filtering, not malformed input. left = cs.split("~")[0] qleft = sum(int(x[1:]) if x[0] == ":" else 1 for x in m.CS.findall(left) if x[0] != "+") cigar = f"{qleft}M" + ("1I" if "+" in left else "") + "100N20M" a = m.parse_sam(sam(start=101-qleft, cigar=cigar, cs=cs)) assert m.call_junctions(a, genome(), "+", "ONT")[0].accepted is accepted

def synthetic_config(tmp_path): def write(name, value): p = tmp_path / name p.write_text(value) return {"path": name, "sha256": m.digest(p)} reference = write("ref.fa", ">chr1
" + genome()["chr1"] + "
") roles = write("roles.tsv", "dataset	run	species	role
" "dataset	run1	synthetic	b1_validation_only
") alignment = write("run.sam", "".join(sam(name=f"r{i}") for i in range(3))) metadata = write("meta.json", json.dumps({f"r{i}": dict( library="lib", bioproject="project", genotype_stratum="reference", ingestion_qc_pass=True, mapping_ambiguous=False, protocol="direct_RNA", umi_status="absent") for i in range(3)})) additions = write("additions.json", json.dumps([m.asdict(addition())])) spec = dict(dataset="dataset", run="run1", species="synthetic", assembly="fixture", source="ONT", genotype_stratum="reference", uf=False, annotation_independence="independent", model_independent=True, status="complete", alignment=alignment, metadata=metadata) config = dict(schema="b1-evidence-v1", purpose="synthetic", assembly="fixture", genome=reference, role_manifests=[roles], additions=additions, runs=[spec]) p = tmp_path / "config.json" p.write_text(json.dumps(config)) return p, config

nodes.body_text: def test_cli_reproducibility_and_hash_tampering(tmp_path): p, config = synthetic_config(tmp_path) assert m.main(["--config", str(p), "--out", str(tmp_path / "out1")]) == 0 assert m.main(["--config", str(p), "--out", str(tmp_path / "out2")]) == 0 one, two = tmp_path / "out1", tmp_path / "out2" assert {f.name: f.read_bytes() for f in one.iterdir()} == {f.name: f.read_bytes() for f in two.iterdir()} provenance = json.loads((one / "PROVENANCE.json").read_text()) assert str(SCRIPT) in provenance["inputs_sha256"] (tmp_path / "run.sam").write_text(sam()) assert m.main(["--config", str(p), "--out", str(tmp_path / "out3")]) == 2 assert not (tmp_path / "out3").exists()

nodes.body_text: def test_pcr_diagnostic_counts_candidates_without_mutating_or_raising(): reads = [obs(f"r{i}", run="run1" if i < 2 else "run2") for i in range(3)] for offset, o in zip((0, 9, 18), reads): o.metadata["protocol"] = "cDNA" o.alignment = replace(o.alignment, start=51+offset, end=400+offset) # A separate clique in the same library/chain is another candidate. far = obs("far") far.metadata["protocol"] = "cDNA" far.alignment = replace(far.alignment, start=700, end=900) specs = [dict(dataset="dataset", run=r, arm="primary") for r in ("run1", "run2", "empty")] additions = [addition(), addition(addition_id="away", locus_start=910, locus_end=990, cds_start=920, cds_end=980, introns=(), novel_introns=(), novelty="reference-alt")] before = [m.asdict(o) for o in reads + [far]] d = m.pcr_diagnostics(reads + [far], additions, specs) assert (d["candidate_equivalence_groups"], d["non_clique_groups"]) == (2, 1) assert [r["non_clique_groups"] for r in d["per_run"]] == [1, 1, 0] assert [r["non_clique_groups"] for r in d["per_addition"]] == [1, 0] assert before == [m.asdict(o) for o in reads + [far]] assert d == m.pcr_diagnostics(list(reversed(reads + [far])), additions, specs) with pytest.raises(m.RuleUnresolved): m.assign_molecules(reads)

uf=none
audit_status=FAIL
") spec["provenance"] = write("run.provenance", "fixture
") spec["orientation_audit"] = write("audit.json", json.dumps(dict(status="FAIL"))) p.write_text(json.dumps(config)) return p, config

nodes.name: test_filter_additions_structurally.py
nodes.body_text: """Tests for 36_filter_additions_structurally.py. The filter's whole value is that it discards a lot while keeping the correct structures, so these tests are written against the two ways that can go wrong: discarding something sound, and keeping something unsound. The supplied prompt must survive unconditionally — filtering it out would delete the annotation the user handed in. """ import importlib.util import sys from pathlib import Path import pytest spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location( "filter_additions", Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "36_filter_additions_structurally.py") mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) sys.modules["filter_additions"] = mod spec.loader.exec_module(mod) # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- fixtures # Coordinate map of the fixture genome. Every case the filter distinguishes needs its own # region, and each spliced case needs its exons to abut its intron exactly — an off-by-one # there silently turns a "canonical intron" case into a non-canonical one. # # 1-6 ATGAAA exon A1 ┐ spliced, complete ORF, canonical intron # 7-16 GTCCCCCCAG intron │ GT..AG # 17-19 TAA exon A2 ┘ A1+A2 = ATGAAATAA # 20-28 ATGAAATAA single-exon complete ORF # 29-37 AAAAAATAA no start codon # 38-43 ATGAAA exon B1 ┐ spliced, complete ORF, NON-canonical intron # 44-53 ATCCCCCCTC intron │ AT..TC # 54-56 TAA exon B2 ┘ B1+B2 = ATGAAATAA # 57-70 C*14 padding SPLICED_CANONICAL = [(1, 6), (17, 19)] SINGLE_EXON_ORF = [(20, 28)] NO_START_CODON = [(29, 37)] SPLICED_NON_CANONICAL = [(38, 43), (54, 56)] @pytest.fixture # ------------------------------------------------------------------- ORF completeness # ------------------------------------------------------------------------ splice sites # ------------------------------------------------------------- the prompt is never filtered # ------------------------------------------------------------------------ bookkeeping # --------------------------------------------------------------------- genome aliasing # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- ORF audit # # The audit exists to catch the failure that produced no exception: a genome whose sequence # names do not join to the annotation's, which makes every predicate return False. So the # tests below check that a sound annotation scores high, an unsound one scores low, and a # non-joining genome is reported as skipped rather than as zero percent.

nodes.name: _fasta
nodes.body_text: def _fasta(path: Path, sequences: dict) -> None: path.write_text("".join(f">{n}\n{s}\n" for n, s in sequences.items()))

nodes.name: _gff3
nodes.body_text: def _gff3(path: Path, loci: list) -> None: lines = ["##gff-version 3"] for locus in loci: seq = locus.get("seq", "Chr1") strand = locus.get("strand", "+") gm = f";GM={locus['gm']}" if locus.get("gm") else "" segs = [s for _t, ss in locus["transcripts"] for s in ss] lines.append(f"{seq}\tsrc\tgene\t{min(s for s, _ in segs)}\t{max(e for _, e in segs)}" f"\t.\t{strand}\t.\tID={locus['gene']}{gm}") for tx, ss in locus["transcripts"]: lines.append(f"{seq}\tsrc\tmRNA\t{min(s for s, _ in ss)}\t{max(e for _, e in ss)}" f"\t.\t{strand}\t.\tID={tx};Parent={locus['gene']}{gm}") for n, (s, e) in enumerate(ss, 1): lines.append(f"{seq}\tsrc\tCDS\t{s}\t{e}\t.\t{strand}\t0\t" f"ID={tx}.c{n};Parent={tx}{gm}") path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")

nodes.name: genome
nodes.signature: def genome(tmp_path): # Every piece is joined with an explicit `+`. Mixing implicit literal concatenation # with `+` here silently regrouped the parts and produced a 135 nt sequence whose # regions no longer matched the map above.
nodes.body_text: def genome(tmp_path): # Every piece is joined with an explicit `+`. Mixing implicit literal concatenation # with `+` here silently regrouped the parts and produced a 135 nt sequence whose # regions no longer matched the map above. parts = [ "ATGAAA", # 1-6 exon A1 "GT" + "C" * 6 + "AG", # 7-16 canonical intron "TAA", # 17-19 exon A2 "ATGAAATAA", # 20-28 single-exon ORF "AAAAAATAA", # 29-37 no start codon "ATGAAA", # 38-43 exon B1 "AT" + "C" * 6 + "TC", # 44-53 NON-canonical intron "TAA", # 54-56 exon B2 "C" * 14, # 57-70 padding ] seq = "".join(parts) assert len(seq) == 70, f"fixture genome is {len(seq)} nt, expected 70" path = tmp_path / "genome.fa" _fasta(path, {"Chr1": seq}) return path

nodes.name: _run
nodes.body_text: def _run(tmp_path, genome, prompt_loci, output_loci, filtered=None): prompt = tmp_path / "prompt.gff3" completed = tmp_path / "completed.gff3" _gff3(prompt, prompt_loci) _gff3(completed, output_loci) return mod.filter_predictions(prompt, completed, genome, filtered)

nodes.name: test_make_training_input_manifest.py
nodes.body_text: """The staging gate of 65_make_training_input_manifest.sh (issue #5 packaging path). The gate this file exercises used to compare BASENAMES only, so a held-out test genome whose content sat under an allowed training-species filename passed it. Four test genomes were found in training_input/genomes/ on the first pass, which is why the gate exists at all; comparing names is not enough once the bundle is assembled by hand. Everything here runs against a miniature bundle built in a tmp_path: nine one-line FASTAs and a manifest carrying their real md5s. The real bundle is 28.9 GB and must never be a test dependency. """ import hashlib import shutil import subprocess from pathlib import Path import pytest SCRIPT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "65_make_training_input_manifest.sh" SPECIES = ("Athaliana", "Bdistachyon", "Gmax", "Osativa", "Ppatens", "Ptrichocarpa", "Sbicolor", "Sitalica", "Vvinifera") HEADER = "species_id\tspecies\ttable_s1_version\tfasta\tfasta_md5\tgff\tgff_md5\tnote\n"

nodes.name: md5
nodes.body_text: def md5(path: Path) -> str: return hashlib.md5(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()

run
nodes.body_text: def run(root: Path): return subprocess.run(["bash", str(root / "make_manifest.sh")], capture_output=True, text=True)

nodes.body_text: def test_valid_bundle_is_accepted_and_writes_a_manifest(tmp_path): root = build_bundle(tmp_path / "training_input") r = run(root) assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr manifest = root / "MANIFEST.tsv" assert manifest.exists() lines = manifest.read_text().splitlines() assert lines[0].split("\t")[0] == "category" assert sum(1 for l in lines if l.startswith("genomes\t")) == 9 assert lines[-1].startswith("TOTAL\t")

Give its content the name of a training genome. (root / "genomes" / "Athaliana_test.fa").write_text(">chr1 Zmays\nACGTZMAYS\n") r = run(root) assert r.returncode == 2 assert "md5 mismatch" in r.stderr assert not (root / "MANIFEST.tsv").exists()

nodes.body_text: def test_awk_header_error_is_not_masked_by_the_row_count_check(tmp_path): """awk's `exit N` still runs END, so an END that calls exit would overwrite the code set in a rule. A bad header must report as a bad header, not as 'not nine species'.""" root = build_bundle(tmp_path / "training_input") mani = root / "manifests" / "b5_species_v1.tsv" mani.write_text(mani.read_text().replace("species_id\t", "WRONG\t", 1)) r = run(root) assert r.returncode == 2 assert "unexpected header" in r.stderr assert "exactly nine" not in r.stderr

nodes.name: inputs
nodes.signature: def inputs(tmp_path, records, panels=None, tiles=None, blocks=None)
nodes.body_text: def inputs(tmp_path, records, panels=None, tiles=None, blocks=None): bam = tmp_path / 'tiny.bam' header = {'HD': {'VN': '1.6', 'SO': 'unsorted'}, 'SQ': [{'SN': 'Chr1', 'LN': 200000}, {'SN': 'Chr2', 'LN': 1000}]} with pysam.AlignmentFile(bam, 'wb', header=header) as fh: for name, start, cigar, flag, ts, chrom in records: r = pysam.AlignedSegment(fh.header) r.query_name, r.flag = name, flag if not flag & 4: r.reference_id = fh.get_tid(chrom) r.reference_start = start r.cigarstring, r.mapping_quality = cigar, 60 if ts is not None: r.set_tag('ts', ts, value_type='A') fh.write(r) panel = tmp_path / 'panels.tsv' with panel.open('w') as fh: writer = csv.writer(fh, delimiter='\t') writer.writerow(COLUMNS) for i, (label, chrom, start, end) in enumerate(panels or [('final', 'Chr1', 101, 200)], 1): writer.writerow([label, i, 'Athaliana', f'g{i}', chrom, start, end, '+', end-start+1, '', 1, 2, 1, '']) corpus = tmp_path / 'corpus.db' with duckdb.connect(str(corpus)) as con: con.execute('CREATE TABLE geneList(rn INT PRIMARY KEY, species_id VARCHAR, chromosome VARCHAR, start INT, fin INT, split VARCHAR, is_rc BOOLEAN)') con.executemany('INSERT INTO geneList VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?)', tiles or [ (1, 'Athaliana', 'Chr1', 350, 1000, 'train', False), (2, 'Athaliana', 'Chr1', 350, 1000, 'valid', False), (3, 'Athaliana', 'Chr1', 350, 1000, 'valid', True), (4, 'Athaliana', 'Chr1', 350, 1000, 'test', False), (5, 'Other', 'Chr1', 350, 1000, 'train', False)]) con.execute('CREATE TABLE tile_blocks(species_id VARCHAR, chromosome VARCHAR, start0 INT, end0 INT, split VARCHAR)') con.executemany('INSERT INTO tile_blocks VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)', blocks or [ ('Athaliana', 'Chr1', 2000, 2100, 'test'), ('Other', 'Chr1', 350, 1000, 'test')]) return dict(bam=bam, panels=panel, corpus_db=corpus, out=tmp_path / 'evidence.db')

nodes.name: build
nodes.body_text: def build(tmp_path, records, **kwargs): args = inputs(tmp_path, records, **kwargs) qc = load_builder().build_c0lite(**args) return duckdb.connect(str(args['out']), read_only=True), qc

nodes.name: test_polishing_scoring.py
nodes.body_text: import importlib.util, sys from pathlib import Path import pytest spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location( "score", Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "32_score_polishing.py") score_mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) sys.modules["score"] = score_mod spec.loader.exec_module(score_mod) # -- judgement calls beyond the brief: real 3-level gene -> mRNA -> CDS hierarchy --- # # The two tests above use the brief's flattened fixture (CDS parented straight to the # "gene" column). GeMoMa, BRAKER3 and EGAPx are real 3-level annotations that already # carry alternative isoforms of their own — the scenarios below exercise that shape # directly with raw GFF3 lines, matching what 30_stage_external_annotations.py writes. # -- UTR-level (CDS+UTR) transition table: N/A unless the input shows real UTR signal -- # -- non-coding features (lnc_RNA / pseudogene / bare "transcript") are excluded ---- # -- fail loudly instead of silently scoring zero ---------------------------------- # -- C2: "correct" against ANY reference transcript vs against the PRIMARY only ----- # -- I3: input<->output paired by GM=, input<->reference one-to-one ---------------- # -- I6: cross-tool denominators reconcile ----------------------------------------- # -- M2: 1-based inclusive coordinate math ------------------------------------------ # -- M4: attribute parsing does not match inside a longer key name ----------------- # -- M7: provenance is recorded in the JSON ----------------------------------------- # -- M6: the 2-level fallback is counted, not just silently used ------------------- # =================================================================================== # Fix round 2 (task-2-findings-round2.md) # =================================================================================== # -- R1: split_predictions/ties_broken_by_structure must reach utr_level too -------- # -- R2: the overlap fallback must not steal an output already claimed via GM= ------ # -- R4: primary_source/provenance report the path actually used ------------------- # -- R5: the tie-break override flag must reset when a later, outright winner appears -- # -- R6: a negative "genes without CDS" is reported as undefined, not negative ------ # -- R7: a row with no Parent at all gets its own message, not the noncoding one ---- # -- R9: attribute parsing tolerates a space after the semicolon -------------------- # -- Task 3: baseline mode reports how far the input already is from the reference, # before any model touches it (no output file involved) --------------------------

nodes.name: _gff
nodes.body_text: def _gff(path, rows): """rows: (seq, feat, start, end, gene, tx)""" with open(path, "w") as fh: for seq, feat, s, e, g, t in rows: attr = f"ID={t};Parent={g}" if feat == "CDS" else f"ID={g}" fh.write(f"{seq}\tx\t{feat}\t{s}\t{e}\t.\t+\t0\t{attr}\n")

nodes.name: test_repair_and_damage_are_counted_separately
nodes.body_text: def test_repair_and_damage_are_counted_separately(tmp_path): ref = tmp_path / "ref.gff3" inp = tmp_path / "in.gff3" out = tmp_path / "out.gff3" # locus A: input wrong, output right -> repaired # locus B: input right, output wrong -> damaged # locus C: input right, output right -> preserved _gff(ref, [("Chr1", "CDS", 100, 200, "A", "A.1"), ("Chr1", "CDS", 500, 600, "B", "B.1"), ("Chr1", "CDS", 900, 1000, "C", "C.1")]) _gff(inp, [("Chr1", "CDS", 100, 190, "A", "A.i"), # wrong end ("Chr1", "CDS", 500, 600, "B", "B.i"), # correct ("Chr1", "CDS", 900, 1000, "C", "C.i")]) # correct _gff(out, [("Chr1", "CDS", 100, 200, "A", "A.o"), # fixed ("Chr1", "CDS", 500, 690, "B", "B.o"), # broken ("Chr1", "CDS", 900, 1000, "C", "C.o")]) # kept r = score_mod.score(inp, out, ref) c = r["cds_level"] assert c["repaired"] == 1 assert c["damaged"] == 1 assert c["preserved_correct"] == 1 assert c["still_wrong"] == 0
