nodes.name: target_collate_fn
nodes.body_text: def target_collate_fn(batch): """Collate function for isoformData (NT encoder, multi-segment). Pads variable-segment-count inputs to the maximum number of segments in the batch, and pads labels to the maximum label length. """ # Unpack batch tuples sequences, attention_masks, global_attention_masks, labels, gm, chr, region_start, region_end = zip(*batch) # Pad sequences: flatten segments, pad to max total length, stack max_segs = max([seq.shape[0] for seq in sequences]) # Max segment count in batch sequences = [seq.flatten() for seq in sequences] # Flatten (num_segs, 1024) → (num_segs*1024,) sequences = [F.pad(seq, (0, max_segs*1024 - seq.shape[0]), value=1) for seq in sequences] # Pad with pad_token_id=1 sequences = torch.stack(sequences) # Pad attention masks to match padded sequence length attention_masks = [mask.flatten() for mask in attention_masks] attention_masks = [F.pad(mask, (0, max_segs*1024 - mask.shape[0]), value=False) for mask in attention_masks] attention_masks = torch.stack(attention_masks) # Pad global attention masks if present if global_attention_masks[0] is not None: global_attention_masks = [mask.flatten() for mask in global_attention_masks] global_attention_masks = [F.pad(mask, (0, max_segs*1024 - mask.shape[0]), value=False) for mask in global_attention_masks] global_attention_masks = torch.stack(global_attention_masks) # Pad labels to max label length in batch if labels: max_len = max([label.shape[1] for label in labels]) labels_padded = [F.pad(label, (0, max_len - label.shape[1])) for label in labels] # Right-pad with 0 labels_padded = torch.cat(labels_padded) # Concatenate along batch dim if labels: return sequences, attention_masks, global_attention_masks, labels_padded, gm, chr, region_start, region_end else: return sequences, attention_masks, global_attention_masks, None, gm, chr, region_start, region_end

nodes.name: hyena_collate_fn
nodes.body_text: def hyena_collate_fn(batch): """Collate function for isoformDataHyena (HyenaDNA encoder, variable-length). Pads variable-length DNA sequences to the maximum length in the batch. LEFT-pads sequences (padding at the beginning) because HyenaDNA's causal convolutions are more stable with trailing real tokens. Labels are RIGHT-padded (padding at the end) as is standard. This is the PRIMARY collate function used during TransGenic training. """ arity = len(batch[0]) if batch else 0 if arity not in (7, 8, 9, 10) or any(len(sample) != arity for sample in batch): raise ValueError('expected a nonempty batch with uniform tuple arity 7, 8, 9 or 10') if arity >= 8: sequences, attention_masks, labels, gm, chr, region_start, region_end, tx_counts = zip(*(sample[:8] for sample in batch)) tx_counts = torch.tensor(tx_counts, dtype=torch.float32) else: # Backward compatibility with 7-element tuples sequences, attention_masks, labels, gm, chr, region_start, region_end = zip(*batch) tx_counts = None # LEFT-pad sequences to the longest sequence in the batch dna_max_len = max([seq.shape[1] for seq in sequences]) if arity >= 9: for sample in batch: t = sample[8] if not isinstance(t, torch.Tensor) or t.dtype != torch.float16 or t.shape != (sample[0].shape[1], 8): raise ValueError('evidence tracks must be float16 [DNA token length, 8]') tracks = torch.stack([F.pad(sample[8], (0, 0, dna_max_len-sample[8].shape[0], 0)) for sample in batch]) sequences = [F.pad(seq, (dna_max_len - seq.shape[1], 0)) for seq in sequences] # Left-pad sequences = torch.cat(sequences) # Stack into (batch_size, max_len) # LEFT-pad attention masks to match max_len = max([mask.shape[1] for mask in attention_masks]) attention_masks = [F.pad(mask, (max_len - mask.shape[1], 0)) for mask in attention_masks] attention_masks = torch.cat(attention_masks) # RIGHT-pad labels to the longest label in the batch if None not in labels: label_max_len = max([label.shape[1] for label in labels]) labels_padded = [F.pad(label, (0, label_max_len - label.shape[1]), value=-100) for label in labels] # Right-pad with ignore index labels_padded = torch.cat(labels_padded) if None not in labels: result = (sequences, attention_masks, labels_padded, gm, chr, region_start, region_end, tx_counts) else: result = (sequences, attention_masks, None, gm, chr, region_start, region_end, None) if arity >= 9: result += (tracks,) if arity == 10: result += ({'rn': torch.tensor([s[9]['rn'] for s in batch], dtype=torch.int64), 'has_evidence': torch.tensor([s[9]['has_evidence'] for s in batch], dtype=torch.bool)},) return result

nodes.name: hyenaMLM_collate_fn
nodes.body_text: def hyenaMLM_collate_fn(batch): """Collate function for MLMDatasetHyena (masked language modeling). Same padding strategy as hyena_collate_fn: left-pad sequences, left-pad masks, left-pad labels (original tokens for reconstruction). """ sequences, attention_masks, labels, gm, chr, region_start, region_end = zip(*batch) # LEFT-pad masked sequences max_len = max([seq.shape[1] for seq in sequences]) sequences = [F.pad(seq, (max_len - seq.shape[1], 0)) for seq in sequences] sequences = torch.cat(sequences) # LEFT-pad attention masks max_len = max([mask.shape[1] for mask in attention_masks]) attention_masks = [F.pad(mask, (max_len - mask.shape[1], 0)) for mask in attention_masks] attention_masks = torch.cat(attention_masks) # LEFT-pad original (unmasked) labels for reconstruction loss max_len = max([label.shape[1] for label in labels]) labels = [F.pad(label, (max_len - label.shape[1], 0)) for label in labels] labels = torch.cat(labels) return sequences, attention_masks, labels, gm, chr, region_start, region_end

nodes.name: segment_collate_fn
nodes.body_text: def segment_collate_fn(batch): """Collate function for segmentationDataset (NT encoder, multi-segment). Pads multi-segment sequences and per-position class tensors for batched segmentation training. """ sequences, attention_masks, labels, organism, chromosome, start, end = zip(*batch) # Pad sequences: flatten segments, pad to max total length, stack max_segs = max([seq.shape[0] for seq in sequences]) sequences = [seq.flatten() for seq in sequences] sequences = [F.pad(seq, (0, max_segs*1024 - seq.shape[0]), value=1) for seq in sequences] sequences = torch.stack(sequences) # Pad attention masks attention_masks = [mask.flatten() for mask in attention_masks] attention_masks = [F.pad(mask, (0, max_segs*1024 - mask.shape[0]), value=False) for mask in attention_masks] attention_masks = torch.stack(attention_masks) # Pad class label tensors (per-position multi-class labels) if labels: max_len = max([label.shape[1] for label in labels]) labels_padded = [F.pad(label, (0, max_len - label.shape[1])) for label in labels] labels_padded = torch.stack(labels_padded) if labels: return sequences, attention_masks, labels_padded, organism, chromosome, start, end else: return sequences, attention_masks, None, organism, chromosome, start, end

nodes.name: hyena_segment_collate_fn
nodes.body_text: def hyena_segment_collate_fn(batch): """Collate function for preprocessedSegmentationDatasetHyena. Pads HyenaDNA-tokenized sequences and per-position class tensors for batched segmentation training. """ sequences, attention_masks, labels, organism, chromosome, start, end = zip(*batch) # LEFT-pad input sequences (HyenaDNA dict format) max_len = max([seq["input_ids"].shape[1] for seq in sequences]) sequences = [F.pad(seq["input_ids"], (max_len - seq["input_ids"].shape[1], 0)) for seq in sequences] sequences = torch.cat(sequences) # LEFT-pad attention masks max_len = max([mask.shape[1] for mask in attention_masks]) attention_masks = [F.pad(mask, (max_len - mask.shape[1], 0)) for mask in attention_masks] attention_masks = torch.cat(attention_masks) # Pad class label tensors if labels: max_len = max([label.shape[1] for label in labels]) labels_padded = [F.pad(label, (0, max_len - label.shape[1])) for label in labels] labels_padded = torch.stack(labels_padded) if labels: return sequences, attention_masks, labels_padded, organism, chromosome, start, end else: return sequences, attention_masks, None, organism, chromosome, start, end

Args: dat: Dataset instance. shuffle: Whether to shuffle data (disabled when sampler is provided). batch_size: Number of samples per batch. pin_memory: Pin CPU tensors in page-locked memory for faster GPU transfer. Set False on unified memory systems (GB10). sampler: Optional custom sampler (disables shuffle when set). num_workers: Number of DataLoader worker processes (0 = main process only). collate_fn: Function to collate/pad a list of samples into a batch. persistent_workers: Keep workers alive between epochs to avoid respawn cost. generator: Optional torch.Generator for deterministic shuffle order. Used for reproducible mid-epoch resume. Returns: Configured DataLoader instance. """ if sampler != None: shuffle = False # Sampler and shuffle are mutually exclusive in PyTorch return DataLoader( dat, shuffle=shuffle, collate_fn=collate_fn, batch_size=batch_size, pin_memory=pin_memory, sampler=sampler, num_workers=num_workers, prefetch_factor=prefetch_factor if num_workers > 0 else None, # Pre-fetch 2 batches per worker persistent_workers=persistent_workers if num_workers > 0 else False, # Only valid with workers generator=generator,)

nodes.name: hisat2_extract_splice_sites_gff3.py
nodes.body_text: #!/usr/bin/env python3 # Modified from HiSat2 to include UTR introns and work with GFF3 formatting # https://github.com/DaehwanKimLab/hisat2/blob/master/hisat2_extract_splice_sites.py from sys import stderr, exit import os from collections import defaultdict as dd, Counter from argparse import ArgumentParser, FileType if __name__ == '__main__': parser = ArgumentParser( description='Extract splice junctions from a GTF file') parser.add_argument('gff_file', nargs='?', type=FileType('r'), help='input GFF file (use "-" for stdin)') parser.add_argument('-v', '--verbose', dest='verbose', action='store_true', help='also print some statistics to stderr') parser.add_argument('-f', '--feature', dest='feature_type', default='exon', help='feature type to extract splice junctions (default: exon)') parser.add_argument('-a', '--add', dest='add', action='store_true', help='Add the splice junctions to the gff. Must sort afterwards.') args = parser.parse_args() if not args.gff_file: parser.print_help() exit(1) extract_splice_sites(args.gff_file, feature_type=args.feature_type, verbose=args.verbose, add=args.add)

nodes.name: extract_splice_sites
nodes.body_text: def extract_splice_sites(gff_file, feature_type='exon', verbose=False, add=False): genes = dd(list) trans = {} # Parse valid exon lines from the GTF file into a dict by transcript_id for line in gff_file: line = line.strip() if not line or line.startswith('#'): continue if '#' in line: line = line.split('#')[0].strip() try: chrom, source, feature, left, right, score, \ strand, frame, attributes = line.split('\t') except ValueError: continue left, right = int(left), int(right) if feature != feature_type or left >= right: continue # Parse the attributes column in GFF3 format values_dict = {} for attr in attributes.split(';'): if attr: key, value = attr.strip().split('=') values_dict[key] = value if 'Parent' not in values_dict: continue # Extract the transcript_id from the Parent attribute (assuming it's a single value) transcript_id = values_dict['Parent'] if transcript_id not in trans: trans[transcript_id] = [chrom, strand, [[left, right]]] # Assuming the gene_id can be deduced from the Parent or ID fields in a related entry if 'ID' in values_dict: gene_id = values_dict['ID'].split('.')[0] else: gene_id = transcript_id.split('.')[0] genes[gene_id].append(transcript_id) else: trans[transcript_id][2].append([left, right]) # Sort spliced features and merge where separating introns are <=5 bps for tran, [chrom, strand, exons] in trans.items(): exons.sort() tmp_exons = [exons[0]] for i in range(1, len(exons)): if exons[i][0] - tmp_exons[-1][1] <= 5: tmp_exons[-1][1] = exons[i][1] else: tmp_exons.append(exons[i]) trans[tran] = [chrom, strand, tmp_exons] # Calculate and print the unique junctions junctions = set() for chrom, strand, exons in trans.values(): for i in range(1, len(exons)): junctions.add((chrom, exons[i-1][1], exons[i][0], strand)) junctions = sorted(junctions) if add: os.system(f"cp {gff_file.name} {gff_file.name.split('gff')[0]}splice.gff3") for chrom, left, right, strand in junctions: # Zero-based offset print('{}\t{}\t{}\t{}'.format(chrom, left-1, right-1, strand)) if add: with open(f"{gff_file.name.split('gff')[0]}splice.gff3", 'a') as f: if strand == '+': donor_start = left + 1 donor_end = left + 2 acceptor_start = right - 2 acceptor_end = right -1 else: donor_start = right - 2 donor_end = right - 1 acceptor_start = left + 1 acceptor_end = left + 2 f.write(f"{chrom}\tHisat2_Splice\tfive_prime_cis_splice_site\t{donor_start}\t{donor_end}\t.\t{strand}\t.\tID=splice_donor_{chrom}_{donor_start}\n") f.write(f"{chrom}\tHisat2_Splice\tthree_prime_cis_splice_site\t{acceptor_start}\t{acceptor_end}\t.\t{strand}\t.\tID=splice_acceptor_{chrom}_{donor_start}\n") # Print some stats if asked if verbose: exon_lengths, intron_lengths, trans_lengths = \ Counter(), Counter(), Counter() for chrom, strand, exons in trans.values(): tran_len = 0 for i, exon in enumerate(exons): exon_len = exon[1]-exon[0]+1 exon_lengths[exon_len] += 1 tran_len += exon_len if i == 0: continue intron_lengths[exon[0] - exons[i-1][1]] += 1 trans_lengths[tran_len] += 1 print('genes: {}, genes with multiple isoforms: {}'.format( len(genes), sum(len(v) > 1 for v in genes.values())), file=stderr) print('transcripts: {}, transcript avg. length: {:.0f}'.format( len(trans), sum(trans_lengths.elements())//len(trans)), file=stderr) print('exons: {}, exon avg. length: {:.0f}'.format( sum(exon_lengths.values()), sum(exon_lengths.elements())//sum(exon_lengths.values())), file=stderr) print('introns: {}, intron avg. length: {:.0f}'.format( sum(intron_lengths.values()), sum(intron_lengths.elements())//sum(intron_lengths.values())), file=stderr) print('average number of exons per transcript: {:.0f}'.format( sum(exon_lengths.values())//len(trans)), file=stderr)

nodes.name: preprocess.py
nodes.body_text: """ DuckDB Database Builder for TransGenic Training and Inference. Converts genome FASTA files and GFF3/BED annotation files into DuckDB databases that serve as the data backend for TransGenic's PyTorch DataLoader pipeline. The main function, genome2GSFDataset(), processes a sorted GFF3 file line-by-line, extracting each gene region with flanking genomic context and converting its annotation to the compact GSF (Gene Sentence Format) string representation. Database Schema (geneList table): rn INT PRIMARY KEY -- Auto-incrementing row ID geneModel VARCHAR -- Gene ID from GFF3 ID= attribute start INT -- 0-indexed region start in chromosome fin INT -- Region end (exclusive, Python-style) strand VARCHAR -- Gene strand: "+" or "-" chromosome VARCHAR -- Chromosome/scaffold name sequence VARCHAR -- Extracted DNA sequence (gene + flanking) gff VARCHAR -- GSF annotation string (NULL in predict mode) static_fpb INT -- Static 5' flanking buffer size (bp) static_tpb INT -- Static 3' flanking buffer size (bp) five_prime_buf INT -- Random 5' offset for training augmentation three_prime_buf INT -- Random 3' offset for training augmentation Key design decisions: - Sequences are padded with flanking genomic context to the nearest multiple of staticSize (default 6144bp), matching the HyenaDNA encoder chunk size. - In training mode, random buffer offsets (addExtra) teach the model to locate UTR boundaries regardless of their position within the input window. - Reverse complement augmentation (addRC) doubles data for splice variant diversity; addRCIsoOnly restricts this to multi-isoform genes. - The clean flag filters genes with invalid CDS (missing start/stop codons or reading frame errors) to ensure training labels are biologically valid. - GFF3 phase values (0/1/2) are remapped to GSF phase tokens (A/B/C). - Feature deduplication ensures that CDS/UTR features shared across alternative transcripts appear only once in the feature list. This module also includes two legacy/auxiliary functions for segmentation tasks: - genome2SegmentationDataset: Stores raw GFF3 + genome in DuckDB (slow) - genome2PreprocessedSegmentationDt: Creates windowed segmentation data with 14-class binary labels for nucleotide-level feature prediction """ import os import sys import zlib import duckdb import torch import pandas as pd from tqdm import tqdm from ..utils.sequence import loadGenome, reverseComplement, validateCDS from ..utils.gsf import reverseComplement_gffString

nodes.name: genome2GSFDataset
nodes.signature: def genome2GSFDataset( genome: str, gff3: str, db: str, anoType = 'gff', mode = 'predict', maxLen=49152, addExtra=0, staticSize=6144, addRC=False, addRCIsoOnly=False, clean=False, speciesPrefix: str = '' )
nodes.body_text: def genome2GSFDataset( genome: str, gff3: str, db: str, anoType = 'gff', mode = 'predict', maxLen=49152, addExtra=0, staticSize=6144, addRC=False, addRCIsoOnly=False, clean=False, speciesPrefix: str = '' ): """ Build a DuckDB database from a genome FASTA and GFF3/BED annotation file. Reads a sorted GFF3 (or BED) file line-by-line, extracts each gene region with flanking genomic context padded to the nearest multiple of staticSize, converts the annotation to GSF format, and inserts the result into a DuckDB database. Can be called multiple times to append multiple genomes. Args: genome (str): Path to genome FASTA file. gff3 (str): Path to sorted GFF3 or BED annotation file. db (str): Path to DuckDB database file (created if not exists). anoType (str): Input format - "gff" for GFF3, "bed" for BED. Default "gff". mode (str): "train" includes GSF labels; "predict" stores only gene regions (skips sub-gene features). Default "predict". maxLen (int): Skip genes whose padded region exceeds this length. Default 49152 (8 x 6144 = max HyenaDNA encoder input). addExtra (int): Max random buffer (bp) added to each side for training augmentation. Helps model learn UTR boundaries. Default 0. staticSize (int): Pad sequences to multiples of this size. Must match the encoder chunk size. Default 6144. addRC (bool): Add reverse complement copies for data augmentation. addRCIsoOnly (bool): When addRC=True, only augment genes with alternative splicing (multiple mRNA transcripts). clean (bool): Validate CDS integrity (start/stop codons, reading frame) before insertion; skip invalid genes. speciesPrefix (str): Prefix to prepend to chromosome names (e.g., "Zm" turns "Chr01" into "Zm_Chr01"). Useful for multi-species databases to avoid chromosome name collisions. Default "". """ # Since 2026-09-02 this function delegates to build_b5.build_species (docs/gsf_spec_v1.md): # the last gene of a file is flushed, exact-multiple windows get no extra chunk, records over the # caps are rejected instead of truncated, inserts are parameterised and the GSF text is canonical # (gsf-order-v1). Legacy columns are unchanged; split/provenance columns are NULL when no split # table is supplied. B5 builds must use scripts/build_b5_database.py with the frozen split table. from .build_b5 import build_species import duckdb as _duckdb if anoType != 'gff': raise NotImplementedError("BED input is no longer supported; convert to GFF3 first") if addRCIsoOnly and not addRC: addRC = True # --add-rc-iso-only alone used to be a silent no-op rc = 'none' if not addRC else ('isoform-only' if addRCIsoOnly else 'all') species_id = speciesPrefix or os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(genome))[0] con = _duckdb.connect(db) try: result = build_species(con, species_id, genome, gff3, split_rows={}, split_sha="", rc=rc, add_extra=addExtra, max_len=maxLen, clean=clean, mode=mode, allow_missing_split=True) finally: con.close() for r in result["rejected"]: print(f"Skipping {r['gene_id']}: {r['reason']}", file=sys.stderr) if staticSize != 6144: print(f"Warning: staticSize={staticSize} ignored; the frozen window policy is sym6144-v1", file=sys.stderr) return result

nodes.name: genome2SegmentationDataset
nodes.body_text: def genome2SegmentationDataset(genome_file, gff_file, organism, db): """ Load raw GFF3 annotations and genome sequences into DuckDB tables. Creates two tables per organism: - {organism}_gff: Full GFF3 annotation rows - {organism}_genome: Chromosome sequences with lengths This is a LEGACY implementation. On-the-fly feature extraction during dataloading is very slow. Use genome2PreprocessedSegmentationDt instead. Args: genome_file (str): Path to genome FASTA file. gff_file (str): Path to GFF3 annotation file. organism (str): Organism name (used as table name prefix). db (str): Path to DuckDB database file. """ # Load GFF3 into a pandas DataFrame and store in DuckDB table = organism gff3 = pd.read_csv(gff_file, sep='\t', header=None, comment='#') gff3.columns = ['chromosome', 'source', 'feature', 'start', 'fin', 'score', 'strand', 'frame', 'attribute'] gff3['organism'] = organism with duckdb.connect(db) as con: con.sql( f'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {table}_gff (' 'chromosome VARCHAR, ' 'source VARCHAR, ' 'feature VARCHAR, ' 'start INT, ' 'fin INT, ' 'score VARCHAR, ' 'strand VARCHAR, ' 'frame VARCHAR, ' 'attribute VARCHAR, ' 'organism VARCHAR)') con.sql( f'INSERT INTO {table}_gff ' 'SELECT * ' 'FROM gff3; ' ) # Load chromosome sequences into DuckDB with length metadata genome_dict = loadGenome(genome_file) genome_df = pd.DataFrame(genome_dict.items(), columns=['chromosome', 'sequence']) genome_df['organism'] = organism genome_df['length'] = genome_df['sequence'].apply(len) with duckdb.connect(db) as con: con.sql( f"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {table}_genome (" 'chromosome VARCHAR, ' 'sequence VARCHAR, ' 'organism VARCHAR, ' 'length INT)') con.sql( f'INSERT INTO {table}_genome ' 'SELECT * ' 'FROM genome_df; ' )

nodes.name: genome2PreprocessedSegmentationDt
nodes.signature: def genome2PreprocessedSegmentationDt(db, genome, gff, table, window_size, step_size)
nodes.body_text: def genome2PreprocessedSegmentationDt(db, genome, gff, table, window_size, step_size): """ Create a pre-processed segmentation dataset with sliding windows. Converts genome + GFF3 into a TSV file where each row is a fixed-size genomic window with a 14-class binary label tensor (zlib-compressed). This pre-computes the nucleotide-level labels once instead of doing it on-the-fly during training, dramatically improving dataloading speed. The 14 segmentation classes are: [0] protein_coding_gene [7] 3UTR [1] lncRNA [8] CTCF-bound [2] exon [9] polyA_signal [3] intron [10] enhancer_Tissue_specific [4] splice_donor [11] enhancer_Tissue_invariant [5] splice_acceptor [12] promoter_Tissue_specific [6] 5UTR [13] promoter_Tissue_invariant Args: db (str): Output TSV file path (appended to). genome (str): Path to genome FASTA file. gff (str): Path to GFF3 annotation file. table (str): Organism/dataset label for the TSV rows. window_size (int): Size of each sliding window (bp). step_size (int): Step between consecutive windows (bp). """ # 14 nucleotide-level segmentation classes for multi-label prediction classes = ['protein_coding_gene', 'lncRNA', 'exon', 'intron', 'splice_donor', 'splice_acceptor', '5UTR', '3UTR', 'CTCF-bound', 'polyA_signal', 'enhancer_Tissue_specific', 'enhancer_Tissue_invariant', 'promoter_Tissue_specific', 'promoter_Tissue_invariant'] # Map GFF3 feature types to segmentation class names gffClassMap = {'gene': 'protein_coding_gene', 'exon': 'exon', 'intron': 'intron', 'five_prime_cis_splice_site': 'splice_donor', 'three_prime_cis_splice_site': 'splice_acceptor', 'five_prime_UTR': '5UTR', 'three_prime_UTR': '3UTR'} # Read genome sequence and GFF3 annotation into memory genome = loadGenome(genome) gff = pd.read_csv(gff, sep='\t', header=None, comment='#') gff.columns = ['chromosome', 'source', 'feature', 'start', 'fin', 'score', 'strand', 'frame', 'attributes'] for chr in genome: # Build a per-nucleotide binary class tensor for this chromosome sequence = genome[chr] chr_gff = gff[gff['chromosome'] == chr].reset_index(drop=True) # Shape: (chromosome_length, 14) -- one-hot per nucleotide per class class_tensor = torch.zeros((len(sequence), len(classes)), dtype=torch.float32) print(f"Processing chr {chr}...", file=sys.stderr) skip = False for i, row in tqdm(chr_gff.iterrows()): start = row['start'] end = row['fin'] feature = row['feature'] # Look ahead to detect lncRNA genes (skip their children) nextfeature = chr_gff.loc[i+1, 'feature'] if i+1 < len(chr_gff) else None if feature == 'gene': skip = False if nextfeature == 'lncRNA': skip = True if not skip: if feature in gffClassMap: # Set the binary label for this class across the feature's span class_idx = classes.index(gffClassMap[feature]) class_tensor[start:end, class_idx] = 1 # Slide a fixed-size window across the chromosome and output each window print(f"Adding {chr} windows...", file=sys.stderr) for i in tqdm(range(0, len(sequence), step_size)): start = i end = i + window_size if end > len(sequence): end = len(sequence) window_seq = sequence[start:end] window_class = class_tensor[start:end] # Compress the label tensor with zlib to reduce file size window_class = zlib.compress(window_class.numpy().tobytes()) # Append as tab-separated: sequence, compressed_labels, organism, chr, start, end with open(db, 'a') as f: f.write(f"{window_seq}\t{window_class}\t{table}\t{chr}\t{start}\t{end}\n")

nodes.name: qc_flags.py
nodes.body_text: """Annotation-quality flag semantics shared by 62_geenuff_qc.py, 63_swissprot_sensitivity.py and build_b5.py (protocols A22, A30). Hard flags mask a gene model from the training loss (train_weight 0) or drop the flagged transcript; every other flag is soft and recorded only. `swissprot_caution_*` (A30: a Swiss-Prot SEQUENCE CAUTION of a structural type whose curated sequence is absent from the current reference proteome) is hard; `swissprot_note_*` is soft.""" HARD_FLAG_PATTERNS = ("missing_start", "missing_stop", "wrong_starting_phase", "mismatched_ending_phase", "mismatched_phase", "overlapping_exon", "too_short_intron", "empty_transcript", "empty_super_locus", "wrong_phase", "super_loci_overlap", "missmatching_strand", "truncated_intron", # GeenuFF 702cbf3 names (inconsistent models) "swissprot_caution")

nodes.name: is_hard
nodes.body_text: def is_hard(flag: str) -> bool: f = flag.lower() return any(p in f for p in HARD_FLAG_PATTERNS)

nodes.name: mvp_bootstrap.py
nodes.body_text: """Paired bootstrap and the §5.3 futility decision for the B6 MVP (exploratory). Pinned statistics contract (B6_MVP_PILOT_v1.md §5.2/§5.3): * delta_loss = loss_off - loss_on (positive = improvement). NEVER on - off. * delta_F1 / delta_P / delta_R = metric_on - metric_off. * Paired TILE bootstrap for the primary: resample tiles with replacement, BOOTSTRAP_REPLICATES = 2,000, numpy.random.default_rng(BOOTSTRAP_SEED = 20260914); a resampled tile carries its three seeds' pairs; one-sided 95% bounds are the 5th/95th percentiles of the replicate means. * Paired LOCUS bootstrap (same replicate count and seed) for delta_F1/P/R. * delta_loss threshold DELTA_LOSS = 0.005 nats; delta_F1 threshold DELTA_F1 = 2.0 percentage points. These constants are frozen: no function here accepts an override, and mvp_score.py refuses CLI attempts to change them. The decision function implements §5.3 verbatim: STOP is evaluated FIRST; GO only if STOP fails; availability safeguards downgrade a prospective STOP to INCONCLUSIVE, never to GO. Record validation mirrors src/transgenic/training/mvp_metrics.py exactly (PAIRED_RECORD fields) without importing torch, so scoring can run on CPU-only nodes; a unit test asserts the field list here matches mvp_metrics. """ import math from dataclasses import dataclass from numbers import Integral, Real import numpy as np # --- frozen constants (spec §5.2/§5.3); no override path exists --- DELTA_LOSS = 0.005 # nats DELTA_F1 = 2.0 # percentage points BOOTSTRAP_REPLICATES = 2000 BOOTSTRAP_SEED = 20260914 EXPECTED_SEEDS = (1, 2, 3) # mirror of mvp_metrics._NUMERIC_FIELDS / _RTOL / _ATOL (unit-tested equal) PAIRED_NUMERIC_FIELDS = ( "loss_off", "loss_on", "composite_loss_off", "composite_loss_on", "ce_numerator_off", "ce_denominator_off", "ce_numerator_on", "ce_denominator_on", ) _RTOL = 1e-6 _ATOL = 1e-8 @dataclass(frozen=True)

nodes.name: BootstrapError
nodes.body_text: class BootstrapError(ValueError): """Invalid statistics inputs must stop the decision, not degrade it."""

nodes.name: _require
nodes.body_text: def _require(condition, message): if not condition: raise BootstrapError(message)

nodes.name: validate_paired_record
nodes.body_text: def validate_paired_record(record): """Fail-closed validation of one eval_pairs record (mvp_metrics schema).""" required = {"rn", "has_evidence", *PAIRED_NUMERIC_FIELDS} _require(isinstance(record, dict) and required.issubset(record), "paired record is missing required fields") _require(not isinstance(record["rn"], bool) and isinstance(record["rn"], Integral), "record rn must be an integer") _require(isinstance(record["has_evidence"], bool), "record has_evidence must be boolean") for field in PAIRED_NUMERIC_FIELDS: value = record[field] _require(not isinstance(value, bool) and isinstance(value, Real) and math.isfinite(float(value)), f"record {field} must be finite numeric") for suffix in ("off", "on"): denominator = float(record[f"ce_denominator_{suffix}"]) _require(denominator > 0, "CE denominators must be positive") _require(math.isclose(float(record[f"loss_{suffix}"]), float(record[f"ce_numerator_{suffix}"]) / denominator, rel_tol=_RTOL, abs_tol=_ATOL), "CE loss disagrees with its numerator and denominator") _require(math.isclose(float(record["ce_denominator_off"]), float(record["ce_denominator_on"]), rel_tol=_RTOL, abs_tol=_ATOL), "off/on CE denominators disagree") return record

nodes.name: build_tiles
nodes.body_text: def build_tiles(records_by_seed, expected_seeds=EXPECTED_SEEDS): """Assemble evidence-positive tiles carrying one pair per seed. `records_by_seed`: {seed: iterable of validated eval_pairs records}. Returns (rns, deltas) with `deltas` a float64 array [n_tiles, n_seeds] of loss_off - loss_on, seed order = sorted(expected_seeds). Fail-closed on any seed missing a tile, disagreeing evidence flags, or duplicate rns. """ seeds = tuple(sorted(expected_seeds)) _require(seeds == EXPECTED_SEEDS, "primary requires exactly seeds 1, 2, 3") _require(tuple(sorted(records_by_seed)) == seeds, f"expected seeds {seeds}, got {tuple(sorted(records_by_seed))}") per_seed = {} evidence_flags = {} for seed in seeds: rows = {} for record in records_by_seed[seed]: validate_paired_record(record) rn = int(record["rn"]) _require(rn not in rows, f"seed {seed}: duplicate rn {rn}") rows[rn] = record flag = record["has_evidence"] _require(evidence_flags.setdefault(rn, flag) == flag, f"rn {rn}: has_evidence disagrees across seeds") per_seed[seed] = rows inventories = {seed: set(rows) for seed, rows in per_seed.items()} first = inventories[seeds[0]] for seed in seeds[1:]: _require(inventories[seed] == first, f"tile inventory mismatch between seeds {seeds[0]} and {seed}") rns = sorted(rn for rn in first if evidence_flags[rn]) _require(rns, "evidence-positive paired subset is empty") deltas = np.array([[float(per_seed[seed][rn]["loss_off"]) - float(per_seed[seed][rn]["loss_on"]) for seed in seeds] for rn in rns], dtype=np.float64) return tuple(rns), deltas

nodes.name: tile_bootstrap
nodes.body_text: def tile_bootstrap(deltas): """Paired tile bootstrap of the primary delta_loss. `deltas`: float64 [n_tiles, n_seeds] of loss_off - loss_on. One tile draw per replicate; the drawn tile carries ALL its seeds' pairs (the pooled and per-seed replicate statistics use the same resampled tile identities). Returns a dict with point estimates and one-sided 95% bounds (5th/95th percentiles of replicate means). """ deltas = np.asarray(deltas, dtype=np.float64) _require(deltas.ndim == 2 and deltas.shape[0] >= 1 and deltas.shape[1] >= 1, "deltas must be [n_tiles, n_seeds]") _require(np.isfinite(deltas).all(), "deltas must be finite") n_tiles = deltas.shape[0] rng = np.random.default_rng(BOOTSTRAP_SEED) index = rng.integers(0, n_tiles, size=(BOOTSTRAP_REPLICATES, n_tiles)) resampled = deltas[index] # [reps, n_tiles, n_seeds] pooled_reps = resampled.mean(axis=(1, 2)) # tile carries its seeds per_seed_reps = resampled.mean(axis=1) # [reps, n_seeds] return { "pooled_point": float(deltas.mean()), "per_seed_point": [float(v) for v in deltas.mean(axis=0)], "pooled_lower95": float(np.percentile(pooled_reps, 5)), "pooled_upper95": float(np.percentile(pooled_reps, 95)), "per_seed_lower95": [float(v) for v in np.percentile(per_seed_reps, 5, axis=0)], "per_seed_upper95": [float(v) for v in np.percentile(per_seed_reps, 95, axis=0)], "n_tiles": int(n_tiles), "replicates": BOOTSTRAP_REPLICATES, "rng_seed": BOOTSTRAP_SEED, "sign_convention": "delta_loss = loss_off - loss_on", }

nodes.name: locus_bootstrap
nodes.body_text: def locus_bootstrap(per_locus, statistic): """Paired locus bootstrap (same replicate count and seed as the tile one). `per_locus`: sequence of per-locus paired records (opaque to this function). `statistic(records) -> float` computes the pooled paired delta (on - off) over a multiset of locus records. Fail-closed if any replicate yields a non-finite statistic (e.g. a zero pooled denominator). """ per_locus = list(per_locus) _require(per_locus, "locus bootstrap requires at least one locus") point = float(statistic(per_locus)) _require(math.isfinite(point), "statistic is not finite on the full panel") n = len(per_locus) rng = np.random.default_rng(BOOTSTRAP_SEED) index = rng.integers(0, n, size=(BOOTSTRAP_REPLICATES, n)) reps = np.empty(BOOTSTRAP_REPLICATES, dtype=np.float64) for i in range(BOOTSTRAP_REPLICATES): value = float(statistic([per_locus[j] for j in index[i]])) _require(math.isfinite(value), f"replicate {i}: statistic not finite") reps[i] = value return { "point": point, "lower95": float(np.percentile(reps, 5)), "upper95": float(np.percentile(reps, 95)), "n_loci": n, "replicates": BOOTSTRAP_REPLICATES, "rng_seed": BOOTSTRAP_SEED, "sign_convention": "delta_metric = metric_on - metric_off", }

nodes.name: DecisionInputs
nodes.body_text: class DecisionInputs: """Everything §5.3 needs, gathered fail-closed by the caller. primary_lower / primary_upper: one-sided 95% bounds of the pooled tile bootstrap (5th/95th percentiles), delta_loss = off - on. seed_points: the three per-seed delta_loss point estimates. delta_f1_lower: one-sided 95% lower bound on delta_F1 (on - off). The secondary readout is computed from the decodes and must exist; there is no "secondary unavailable" state. structural_available: whether junction P/R against locally aligned A-ONT1/A-HiFi reads exists (spec day-5 availability clause is an availability FACT recorded by the caller, not a wall-clock trigger). delta_r_lower / delta_p_point: junction recall lower bound and precision point estimate; required when structural_available. INTERPRETIVE NOTE (recorded for author review): the spec's contradiction clause "above 0 on delta_R with delta_P not below 0" is implemented as delta_R one-sided 95% lower bound > 0 AND the delta_P POINT ESTIMATE >= 0; the bound reading applies to delta_R (parallel to delta_F1), while "not below 0" on delta_P is read as the point estimate since no bound side is named. withholding_state: "assessed" or "unassessable" (§5.4; assessed only on the provisional-STOP path — pass "unassessable" when no run and no substantiated equivalence argument exists). withholding_primary_upper: when assessed, the sensitivity re-run's primary upper bound; reversal means it is >= DELTA_LOSS. """ primary_lower: float primary_upper: float seed_points: tuple delta_f1_lower: float structural_available: bool delta_r_lower: float = None delta_p_point: float = None withholding_state: str = "unassessable" withholding_primary_upper: float = None

nodes.name: decide
nodes.body_text: def decide(inputs): """§5.3 decision, STOP-first; returns (decision, trace list of strings).""" _require(isinstance(inputs, DecisionInputs), "DecisionInputs required") for name in ("primary_lower", "primary_upper", "delta_f1_lower"): value = getattr(inputs, name) _require(not isinstance(value, bool) and isinstance(value, Real) and math.isfinite(float(value)), f"{name} must be finite numeric") _require(float(inputs.primary_lower) <= float(inputs.primary_upper), "primary bounds are inverted") seeds = tuple(inputs.seed_points) _require(len(seeds) == len(EXPECTED_SEEDS) and all( not isinstance(v, bool) and isinstance(v, Real) and math.isfinite(float(v)) for v in seeds), "exactly three finite seed-level primary point estimates are required") _require(isinstance(inputs.structural_available, bool), "structural_available must be an explicit boolean") if inputs.structural_available: for name in ("delta_r_lower", "delta_p_point"): value = getattr(inputs, name) _require(not isinstance(value, bool) and isinstance(value, Real) and math.isfinite(float(value)), f"{name} required when the structural readout is available") _require(inputs.withholding_state in ("assessed", "unassessable"), "withholding_state must be 'assessed' or 'unassessable'") if inputs.withholding_state == "assessed": value = inputs.withholding_primary_upper _require(not isinstance(value, bool) and isinstance(value, Real) and math.isfinite(float(value)), "assessed withholding requires its primary upper bound") trace = [] prospective_stop = float(inputs.primary_upper) < DELTA_LOSS trace.append(f"primary_upper={float(inputs.primary_upper):.6g} " f"{'<' if prospective_stop else '>='} delta_loss={DELTA_LOSS}: " f"prospective STOP {'holds' if prospective_stop else 'fails'}") stop_failed = not prospective_stop if prospective_stop: contradiction = False if float(inputs.delta_f1_lower) > 0: contradiction = True trace.append("contradiction: delta_F1 one-sided 95% lower bound > 0") if (inputs.structural_available and float(inputs.delta_r_lower) > 0 and float(inputs.delta_p_point) >= 0): contradiction = True trace.append("contradiction: delta_R lower bound > 0 with delta_P " "not below 0") reversal = (inputs.withholding_state == "assessed" and float(inputs.withholding_primary_upper) >= DELTA_LOSS) if reversal: trace.append("withholding reversal: sensitivity primary upper bound " f">= delta_loss={DELTA_LOSS}; STOP fails") if contradiction or reversal: stop_failed = True else: if not inputs.structural_available: trace.append("availability safeguard: structural readout missing; " "prospective STOP downgraded to INCONCLUSIVE (never GO)") return "INCONCLUSIVE", trace if inputs.withholding_state == "unassessable": trace.append("availability safeguard: §5.4 withholding unassessable; " "prospective STOP downgraded to INCONCLUSIVE (never GO)") return "INCONCLUSIVE", trace trace.append("STOP: primary upper bound below delta_loss, no available " "readout contradicts, withholding assessed without reversal") return "STOP", trace if stop_failed: go = (float(inputs.primary_lower) > 0 and all(float(v) > 0 for v in seeds)) if go: trace.append("GO: STOP failed, primary lower bound > 0 and all three " "seed-level delta_loss point estimates positive") return "GO", trace trace.append("INCONCLUSIVE: STOP failed and the GO criteria do not hold") return "INCONCLUSIVE", trace raise AssertionError("unreachable")

nodes.name: mvp_decode.py
nodes.body_text: """Fail-closed MVP model/generation boundaries; panel publication adapter is separate.""" from __future__ import annotations import json from pathlib import Path import re import torch from . import mvp_windows as w LENGTH = 30720 MAX_LENGTH = 8192

nodes.name: require
nodes.body_text: def require(ok, message): if not ok: raise ValueError(message)

nodes.name: read_json
nodes.body_text: def read_json(path): def unique(items): result = {} for key, value in items: require(key not in result, f'duplicate JSON key: {key}') result[key] = value return result return json.loads(Path(path).read_text(), object_pairs_hook=unique)

nodes.name: unique
nodes.body_text: def unique(items): result = {} for key, value in items: require(key not in result, f'duplicate JSON key: {key}') result[key] = value return result

nodes.name: identity
nodes.body_text: def identity(path): path = Path(path).resolve(strict=True) return dict(path=str(path), sha256=w.sha256_file(path), size=path.stat().st_size)

nodes.name: checked_file
nodes.body_text: def checked_file(record): actual = identity(record['path']) require(actual['sha256'] == record['sha256'], 'input SHA256 mismatch') if 'size' in record: require(actual['size'] == record['size'], 'input size mismatch') return actual

nodes.name: encode_window
nodes.body_text: def encode_window(sequence, tokenizer): require(len(sequence) == LENGTH, 'evaluation sequence must be 30720 genomic-forward bases') ids = tokenizer(sequence, return_tensors='pt', truncation=False)['input_ids'] require(ids.shape == (1, LENGTH + 1), 'encoder must yield one base per token plus SEP') require(tokenizer.sep_token_id is not None and ids[0,-1].item() == tokenizer.sep_token_id, 'missing trailing SEP') ids = ids[:, :-1] return ids, ids != tokenizer.pad_token_id

nodes.name: validate_decode
nodes.body_text: def validate_decode(ids, tokenizer): from transgenic.utils import gsf_contract as gc, gsf_grammar ids = list(ids) require(3 <= len(ids) <= MAX_LENGTH and all(type(i) is int for i in ids), 'invalid or truncated raw IDs') vocab = tokenizer.get_vocab() inverse = {v:k for k,v in vocab.items()} require(all(i in inverse for i in ids), 'unknown token ID') tokens = [inverse[i] for i in ids] require(tokens[0] == '<s>' and tokens[-1] == '</s>' and '</s>' not in tokens[1:-1], 'missing/extra EOS or invalid start') for i in range(1,len(tokens)): require(tokens[i] in gsf_grammar.allowed_next(tokens[:i], LENGTH, v2=True, v3=True), f'grammar violation at token {i}') gsf = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_string(tokens[1:-1]) gc.check_caps_v3(gsf, window_len=LENGTH) # Compare, never replace: canonicalization merges duplicate isoforms. require(gc.canonicalize_v3(gsf) == gsf, 'noncanonical GSF (including duplicate isoforms)') return dict(raw_token_ids=ids, raw_tokens=tokens, grammar_plan=[t for t in tokens if re.fullmatch(r'<tx\d+>', t)], gsf=gsf)

nodes.name: validate_gff
nodes.body_text: def validate_gff(text): require(text.startswith('##gff-version 3\n'), 'completed GFF requires exact header') ids, parents = {}, [] for line in text.splitlines()[1:]: require(bool(line) and not line.startswith('#'), 'unexpected empty/comment GFF row') cols = line.split('\t') require(len(cols) == 9, 'invalid GFF columns') attrs = {} for item in cols[8].split(';'): require('=' in item, 'invalid GFF attribute') key, value = item.split('=', 1) require(key not in attrs and re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+', value), 'noncanonical GFF ID/attribute') attrs[key] = value require('ID' in attrs and attrs['ID'] not in ids, 'missing/duplicate GFF ID') require(cols[2] in ('gene','mRNA','exon','CDS','five_prime_UTR','three_prime_UTR'), 'unsupported GFF feature') require(cols[6] in ('+','-') and 1 <= int(cols[3]) <= int(cols[4]), 'invalid genomic coordinates/strand') ids[attrs['ID']] = cols if cols[2] == 'gene': require('Parent' not in attrs, 'gene cannot have Parent') else: require('Parent' in attrs, 'missing Parent') parents.append((attrs['ID'],attrs['Parent'])) for child, parent in parents: require(parent in ids, 'missing parent ID') c, p = ids[child], ids[parent] require(p[2] == ('gene' if c[2] == 'mRNA' else 'mRNA'), 'invalid hierarchy') require(c[0] == p[0] and c[6] == p[6] and int(p[3]) <= int(c[3]) <= int(c[4]) <= int(p[4]), 'parent containment mismatch') return ids

nodes.name: gsf_gff
nodes.body_text: def gsf_gff(gsf, chromosome, start, prefix): from transgenic.utils import gsf_contract as gc from transgenic.utils.gsf import gffString2GFF3 require(re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+', prefix) and re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+', chromosome), 'unsafe identifier') try: gc.check_caps_v3(gsf, window_len=LENGTH) require(gc.canonicalize_v3(gsf) == gsf, 'noncanonical/duplicate GSF') lines = [] for n, block in enumerate(gc.split_v3(gsf), 1): features, txs, strand = gc._parse(block) require(strand in ('+','-') and all(0 <= s < e <= LENGTH and (kind != 'CDS' or e-s >= 3) for kind,s,e,ph in features.values()), 'invalid feature coordinates') rows = gffString2GFF3(block, chromosome, start, 'source=mvp') require(all(rows) and sum('\tmRNA\t' in row for row in rows) == len(txs), 'legacy converter dropped transcript') old = rows[0].split('\t')[8].split(';')[0].removeprefix('ID=') new = f'{prefix}.g{n}' for row in rows: cols = row.split('\t') attrs = cols[8].split(';') cols[8] = ';'.join(k+'='+ (new+v[len(old):] if k in ('ID','Parent') and (v == old or v.startswith(old+'.')) else v) for k,v in (a.split('=',1) for a in attrs)) lines.append('\t'.join(cols)) text = '##gff-version 3\n' + ''.join(line+'\n' for line in lines) validate_gff(text) return text except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError) as error: raise ValueError('malformed GSF') from error

nodes.name: generate_one
nodes.signature: def generate_one(model, tokenizer, input_ids, attention_mask, tracks, *, raw_sink=None)
nodes.body_text: def generate_one(model, tokenizer, input_ids, attention_mask, tracks, *, raw_sink=None): from transformers import GenerationConfig, LogitsProcessorList from transgenic.model.constrained_decoding import GSFGrammarLogitsProcessor require(input_ids.shape == attention_mask.shape == (1,LENGTH), 'invalid sequence batch') require(tracks.shape == (1,LENGTH,8) and tracks.is_floating_point() and torch.isfinite(tracks).all(), 'invalid evidence batch') require(tracks.device == input_ids.device == attention_mask.device, 'batch device mismatch') processor = GSFGrammarLogitsProcessor(tokenizer, [LENGTH], num_beams=2, v2=True, v3=True) model.eval() received = [] hook = model.get_encoder().register_forward_pre_hook( lambda module, args, kwargs: received.append(kwargs.get('evidence_tracks')), with_kwargs=True) try: with torch.inference_mode(): output = model.generate(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask, evidence_tracks=tracks, decoder_input_ids=torch.tensor([[tokenizer.get_vocab()['<s>']]], device=input_ids.device), decoder_start_token_id=tokenizer.get_vocab()['<s>'], num_beams=2, do_sample=False, use_cache=True, max_length=MAX_LENGTH, generation_config=GenerationConfig(), num_return_sequences=1, eos_token_id=tokenizer.get_vocab()['</s>'], pad_token_id=tokenizer.get_vocab()['<pad>'], logits_processor=LogitsProcessorList([processor])) finally: hook.remove() require(len(received) == 1 and received[0] is not None and torch.equal(received[0], tracks), 'generation did not forward evidence exactly once to encoder') require(output.ndim == 2 and output.shape[0] == 1, 'expected one top-beam sequence') ids = output[0].cpu().tolist() if raw_sink is not None: inverse = {v:k for k,v in tokenizer.get_vocab().items()} tokens = [inverse.get(i, '<unknown-ID>') for i in ids] raw_sink(dict(raw_token_ids=ids, raw_tokens=tokens, grammar_plan=[t for t in tokens if re.fullmatch(r'<tx\d+>', t)])) return validate_decode(ids, tokenizer)

nodes.name: load_final_model
nodes.body_text: def load_final_model(verified_run, device='cpu'): """Caller must verify publication; independently parse config and strictly load aliases.""" from safetensors.torch import load_model from transgenic.model.configuration_transgenic import HyenaTransgenicConfig from transgenic.model.modeling_HyenaTransgenic import transgenicForConditionalGeneration files = verified_run['files'] config_file = checked_file(files['config.json']) weights = checked_file(files['model.safetensors']) raw = read_json(config_file['path']) require(raw.get('evidence_channels') == 8 and type(raw.get('evidence_channels')) is int, 'final must have eight evidence channels') require(raw.get('vocab_size') == 290 and raw.get('max_decoder_position_embeddings') == MAX_LENGTH, 'final must use v3/A27 config') config = HyenaTransgenicConfig(**raw) if 'metadata.json' in files: metadata = read_json(checked_file(files['metadata.json'])['path']) target = metadata['initialization_audit']['audit']['target_semantics']['fields'] for name, record in target.items(): require(getattr(config, name, None) == record['value'], f'final config/audit mismatch: {name}') # This construction-only switch prevents external pretrained loading. All # learned tensors (including projection) then come from strict final bytes. pretrained = config.load_pretrained_encoder config.load_pretrained_encoder = False model = transgenicForConditionalGeneration(config) config.load_pretrained_encoder = pretrained load_model(model, weights['path'], strict=True, device='cpu') checked_file(files['model.safetensors']) checked_file(files['config.json']) return model.to(device).eval()

nodes.name: load_baseline_model

nodes.name: mvp_tracks.py
nodes.body_text: """CPU-only eight-channel EST tracks for the exploratory Athaliana MVP. The caller owns a read-only DuckDB connection. Sequence is already output-oriented; offset is always genomic, zero-based. No corpus, torch, sampler or model imports. """ from functools import lru_cache from hashlib import blake2b import math from numbers import Integral import numpy as np

nodes.name: rasterise_est
nodes.signature: def rasterise_est(con, *, sequence, chrom, offset, L, is_rc, keep_fraction, aug_seed, rn=None, population='retained', source_supplied=True)
nodes.body_text: def rasterise_est(con, *, sequence, chrom, offset, L, is_rc, keep_fraction, aug_seed, rn=None, population='retained', source_supplied=True): """Return float16 [L,8]; dropped/zero-fraction source has availability zero. rn restricts to tile_est membership (retained train/valid only). Evaluation windows must omit rn and select population='excluded_heldout'. Separate block and junction queries prevent losing boundaries in intron-only windows. """ if (not isinstance(L,Integral) or L < 0 or not isinstance(offset,Integral) or offset < 0 or not isinstance(sequence,str) or len(sequence) != L): raise ValueError('sequence length must equal nonnegative L; offset must be nonnegative integer') if not math.isfinite(keep_fraction) or not 0 <= keep_fraction <= 1: raise ValueError('keep_fraction must be finite and in [0,1]') if population not in ('retained','excluded_heldout'): raise ValueError('population must be retained or excluded_heldout') result = np.zeros((L,8),dtype=np.float32) if not source_supplied or keep_fraction == 0 or L == 0: return result.astype(np.float16) result[:,7] = 1 @lru_cache(maxsize=None) def keep(molecule_id): rank = int.from_bytes(blake2b(f'{aug_seed}\tAthaliana\t{molecule_id}'.encode(),digest_size=8).digest(),'big') / 2**64 return rank < keep_fraction policy = 'NOT m.excluded' if population == 'retained' else "m.excluded AND m.cause='heldout_locus'" policy += ' AND m.primary_count>0' params = [chrom,offset+L,offset] if rn is not None: policy += ' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tile_est t WHERE t.molecule_id=m.molecule_id AND t.rn=?)' params.append(rn) def rows(sql, args): cur = con.execute(sql,args) while True: batch = cur.fetchmany(4096) if not batch: break yield from batch diff = np.zeros((L+1,3),dtype=np.int64) # Defensively union each molecule's clipped blocks even for a hand-built DB. previous = None lo = hi = channel = None sql = f'''SELECT m.molecule_id,m.strand,b.start0,b.end0 FROM est_block b JOIN est_molecule m USING(molecule_id) WHERE b.chrom=? AND b.start0<? AND b.end0>? AND {policy} ORDER BY m.molecule_id,b.start0,b.end0''' for mid,strand,a,b in rows(sql,params): if not keep(mid): continue a,b = max(a-offset,0),min(b-offset,L) if mid == previous and a <= hi: hi = max(hi,b) else: if previous is not None: diff[lo,channel] += 1 diff[hi,channel] -= 1 previous,lo,hi,channel = mid,a,b,{'+':0,'-':1,'?':2}[strand] if previous is not None: diff[lo,channel] += 1 diff[hi,channel] -= 1 result[:,:3] = np.log1p(np.minimum(np.cumsum(diff[:-1],axis=0),64)) # Endpoint overlap, independent of blocks. Distinct molecule counts at a # boundary even when two different introns share that donor or acceptor. counts = np.zeros((L,4),dtype=np.int64) jparams = [chrom,offset,offset+L,offset,offset+L] if rn is not None: jparams.append(rn) sql = f'''SELECT m.molecule_id,m.strand,j.donor0,j.acceptor0 FROM est_junction j JOIN est_molecule m USING(molecule_id) WHERE j.chrom=? AND ((j.donor0>=? AND j.donor0<?) OR (j.acceptor0>=? AND j.acceptor0<?)) AND {policy} ORDER BY m.molecule_id''' previous,seen = None,set() for mid,strand,donor,acceptor in rows(sql,jparams): if strand == '?' or not keep(mid): continue if previous != mid: seen.clear() previous = mid for position,channel in ((donor,0 if strand=='+' else 2),(acceptor,1 if strand=='+' else 3)): if position is not None and offset <= position < offset+L: key = (position-offset,channel) if key not in seen: np.add.at(counts,key,1) seen.add(key) result[:,3:7] = np.log1p(counts) if is_rc: result = result[::-1][:,[1,0,2,5,6,3,4,7]] # Mask LAST: sequence is already RC-oriented when is_rc=True. bases = np.frombuffer(sequence.encode('ascii'),dtype=np.uint8) result[(bases==ord('N')) | (bases==ord('n'))] = 0 return np.ascontiguousarray(result,dtype=np.float16)

nodes.name: mvp_windows.py
nodes.body_text: """Shared MVP panel window derivation and restriction predicates (B6_MVP_PILOT_v1 §1.2/§2). This module is the single source of the 30,720-nt evaluation-window definition. Every consumer — the decoder, the pass-1 long-read prefilter, the junction table, and the scoring restriction predicates — must derive windows from here so that the window used for scoring is exactly the window that was decoded (Track B review must-fix 1). Coordinate conventions ---------------------- * Panel TSV `start`/`fin` are 1-based inclusive (spec §1.2). We convert once to half-open 0-based `[gene_start0, gene_end0)` and never mix conventions. * Evaluation window: WINDOW_LENGTH = 30,720 nt CENTRED on the gene. With ``pad_total = WINDOW_LENGTH - gene_length`` the left pad is ``pad_total // 2`` and the right pad is ``pad_total - pad_total // 2`` (the odd base goes to the genomic right). This is deterministic and documented here once. * Prefilter interval: window +/- PREFILTER_PAD. The spec text says "panel windows ± 10 kb"; "10 kb" is resolved as the decimal 10,000 nt, NOT 10,240 (the 10,240 figure appearing elsewhere is a tile-geometry constant, not the spec's prefilter pad). Frozen here as PREFILTER_PAD = 10_000. * Junction intron coordinates are 0-based INCLUSIVE endpoints (`intron_start0`, `intron_end0`), matching the C0-lite `est_junction` table. Two restriction scopes (must-fix 2) — do not conflate them: * READ-SUPPORTED junctions are counted inside panel WINDOWS (`junction_within_windows`, containment in the 30,720-nt window). * PREDICTED junctions and the recall denominator are restricted against panel GENES (`transcript_overlaps_gene` for selecting decoded transcripts, `junction_within_genes` for the read-supported recall denominator). Fail-closed: a window that would extend beyond the chromosome (or below 0) is an error, never a silent clamp/shift; that case needs an author decision. """ import csv import hashlib from dataclasses import dataclass from pathlib import Path WINDOW_LENGTH = 30_720 PREFILTER_PAD = 10_000 # spec "10 kb" == 10,000 nt (decimal); NOT 10,240. # Commit-bound trust anchor: sha256 of revision/protocols/b6_panels_v1.tsv at # f847cb80c7750326f0781f81481891ab0c9ea309 (matches the committed .sha256 # companion; verified by the Track B adversarial review). PANEL_SHA256 = "79367154bbf922fd0554285cb6cb47ae3d3c866b145aa1f51ead4f47b00cd243" PANEL_COLUMNS = ( "panel", "shuffle_rank", "species_id", "gene_id", "chromosome", "start", "fin", "strand", "length", "orthogroup_id", "n_transcripts", "exon_count", "intron_count", "est_molecules", ) MVP_LABELS = ("mvp_core", "mvp") MVP_EXPECTED_COUNTS = {"mvp_core": 20, "mvp": 30} @dataclass(frozen=True)

nodes.name: sha256_file
nodes.body_text: def sha256_file(path): h = hashlib.sha256() with open(path, "rb") as f: for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""): h.update(block) return h.hexdigest()

nodes.name: load_panel
nodes.body_text: def load_panel(path, expected_sha256=PANEL_SHA256, labels=MVP_LABELS): """Load the MVP panel loci fail-closed. The default `expected_sha256` pins the commit-bound b6_panels_v1.tsv hash; tests may pass the hash of a fixture explicitly, but there is no way to skip the check. """ path = Path(path) _require(isinstance(expected_sha256, str) and len(expected_sha256) == 64, "an explicit expected sha256 is required") actual = sha256_file(path) _require(actual == expected_sha256, f"panel TSV hash mismatch: {path} has {actual}, expected {expected_sha256}") loci = [] with open(path, newline="") as f: reader = csv.reader(f, delimiter="\t") header = tuple(next(reader)) _require(header == PANEL_COLUMNS, f"panel TSV header mismatch: {header!r}") for row in reader: _require(len(row) == len(PANEL_COLUMNS), f"panel row has {len(row)} fields") record = dict(zip(PANEL_COLUMNS, row)) if record["panel"] not in labels: continue start1, fin1, length = (int(record["start"]), int(record["fin"]), int(record["length"])) _require(1 <= start1 <= fin1, f"{record['gene_id']}: invalid start/fin") _require(length == fin1 - start1 + 1, f"{record['gene_id']}: length column disagrees with start/fin") _require(record["strand"] in ("+", "-"), f"{record['gene_id']}: invalid strand") loci.append(PanelLocus(record["panel"], record["gene_id"], record["chromosome"], start1, fin1, record["strand"], length)) counts = {} for locus in loci: counts[locus.panel] = counts.get(locus.panel, 0) + 1 if set(labels) == set(MVP_LABELS): _require(counts == MVP_EXPECTED_COUNTS, f"MVP panel counts {counts} != {MVP_EXPECTED_COUNTS}") _require(len({(l.chromosome, l.gene_id) for l in loci}) == len(loci), "duplicate panel gene") return tuple(loci)

nodes.name: evaluation_window
nodes.body_text: def evaluation_window(locus, chrom_length=None): """30,720-nt half-open window `[w_start0, w_end0)` centred on the gene. This is THE window the decoder decodes and the scorer restricts to. Fail-closed at chromosome edges: no silent clamping. """ gene_len = locus.gene_end0 - locus.gene_start0 _require(gene_len == locus.length, f"{locus.gene_id}: inconsistent gene length") _require(gene_len <= WINDOW_LENGTH, f"{locus.gene_id}: gene length {gene_len} exceeds window {WINDOW_LENGTH}") pad_total = WINDOW_LENGTH - gene_len pad_left = pad_total // 2 # odd base goes to the genomic right w_start0 = locus.gene_start0 - pad_left w_end0 = w_start0 + WINDOW_LENGTH _require(w_start0 >= 0, f"{locus.gene_id}: evaluation window would start before the chromosome " f"({w_start0}); author decision required, no silent clamp") if chrom_length is not None: _require(w_end0 <= chrom_length, f"{locus.gene_id}: evaluation window would end past the chromosome; " f"author decision required, no silent clamp") return (w_start0, w_end0)

nodes.name: prefilter_interval
nodes.body_text: def prefilter_interval(window): """Pass-1 candidate-read interval: evaluation window +/- 10,000 nt. The left edge is floored at 0 — the PREFILTER is a superset selector, so flooring can only keep extra reads, never drop evaluation-window evidence (unlike the window itself, which is fail-closed). """ w_start0, w_end0 = window _require(w_end0 - w_start0 == WINDOW_LENGTH, "not an evaluation window") return (max(0, w_start0 - PREFILTER_PAD), w_end0 + PREFILTER_PAD)

nodes.name: windows_by_chromosome
nodes.body_text: def windows_by_chromosome(loci, chrom_lengths=None): """Map chromosome -> sorted list of evaluation windows (half-open).""" result = {} for locus in loci: length = None if chrom_lengths is None else chrom_lengths[locus.chromosome] result.setdefault(locus.chromosome, []).append(evaluation_window(locus, length)) return {chrom: sorted(spans) for chrom, spans in result.items()}

nodes.name: prefilter_by_chromosome
nodes.body_text: def prefilter_by_chromosome(loci): """Map chromosome -> sorted list of pass-1 prefilter intervals (half-open).""" result = {} for locus in loci: result.setdefault(locus.chromosome, []).append( prefilter_interval(evaluation_window(locus))) return {chrom: sorted(spans) for chrom, spans in result.items()}

nodes.name: _contained
nodes.body_text: def _contained(span_start0, span_end0_incl, intervals): """0-based-inclusive span fully inside any half-open interval.""" _require(span_start0 <= span_end0_incl, "invalid span") return any(start0 <= span_start0 and span_end0_incl < end0 for start0, end0 in intervals)

nodes.name: _overlapping
nodes.body_text: def _overlapping(span_start0, span_end0_incl, intervals): """0-based-inclusive span overlapping any half-open interval by >= 1 base.""" _require(span_start0 <= span_end0_incl, "invalid span") return any(span_start0 < end0 and span_end0_incl >= start0 for start0, end0 in intervals)

nodes.name: junction_within_windows
nodes.body_text: def junction_within_windows(chrom, intron_start0, intron_end0, windows): """Scope 1 (must-fix 2): READ-SUPPORTED junctions count inside panel WINDOWS. `windows` is the mapping from `windows_by_chromosome`. Containment of the 0-based inclusive intron span in the 30,720-nt window. """ return _contained(intron_start0, intron_end0, windows.get(chrom, ()))

nodes.name: genes_by_chromosome
nodes.body_text: def genes_by_chromosome(loci): """Map chromosome -> sorted list of half-open gene spans.""" result = {} for locus in loci: result.setdefault(locus.chromosome, []).append( (locus.gene_start0, locus.gene_end0)) return {chrom: sorted(spans) for chrom, spans in result.items()}

nodes.name: junction_within_genes
nodes.body_text: def junction_within_genes(chrom, intron_start0, intron_end0, genes): """Scope 2a (must-fix 2): recall DENOMINATOR — read-supported junctions inside the panel GENES (containment in the gene span, spec §2 'inside the panel genes'). `genes` is the mapping from `genes_by_chromosome`.""" return _contained(intron_start0, intron_end0, genes.get(chrom, ()))

nodes.name: transcript_overlaps_gene
nodes.body_text: def transcript_overlaps_gene(chrom, tx_start0, tx_end0_incl, genes): """Scope 2b (must-fix 2): PREDICTED junctions come from decoded transcripts OVERLAPPING the panel gene (spec §2 'introns of the decoded transcripts overlapping the panel gene'): >= 1 base of transcript-span overlap.""" return _overlapping(tx_start0, tx_end0_incl, genes.get(chrom, ()))

nodes.body_text: class TransgenicConfig(PretrainedConfig): r""" This is the configuration class to store the configuration of a [`transgenicModel`]. It is used to instantiate an Transgenic model according to the specified arguments, defining the model architecture. Instantiating a configuration with the defaults will yield a similar configuration to that of the LED [jlomas/transgenic-agro-E9](https://huggingface.co/jlomas/transgenic-agro-E9) architecture. Configuration objects inherit from [`PretrainedConfig`] and can be used to control the model outputs. Read the documentation from [`PretrainedConfig`] for more information. Args: vocab_size (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 272): Vocabulary size of the Transgenic model. Defines the number of different tokens that can be represented by the `decoder_inputs_ids` passed when calling [`transgenicModel`]. d_model (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 1024): Dimensionality of the layers and the pooler layer. encoder_layers (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 12): Number of encoder layers. decoder_layers (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 12): Number of decoder layers. encoder_attention_heads (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 16): Number of attention heads for each attention layer in the Transformer encoder. decoder_attention_heads (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 16): Number of attention heads for each attention layer in the Transformer decoder. decoder_ffn_dim (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 4096): Dimensionality of the "intermediate" (often named feed-forward) layer in decoder. encoder_ffn_dim (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 4096): Dimensionality of the "intermediate" (often named feed-forward) layer in decoder. activation_function (`str` or `function`, *optional*, defaults to `"gelu"`): The non-linear activation function (function or string) in the encoder and pooler. If string, `"gelu"`, `"relu"`, `"silu"` and `"gelu_new"` are supported. dropout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.1): The dropout probability for all fully connected layers in the embeddings, encoder, and pooler. attention_dropout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.0): The dropout ratio for the attention probabilities. activation_dropout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.0): The dropout ratio for activations inside the fully connected layer. classifier_dropout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.0): The dropout ratio for classifier. max_encoder_position_embeddings (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 16384): The maximum sequence length that the encoder might ever be used with. max_decoder_position_embeddings (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 16384): The maximum sequence length that the decoder might ever be used with. init_std (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.02): The standard deviation of the truncated_normal_initializer for initializing all weight matrices. encoder_layerdrop (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.0): The LayerDrop probability for the encoder. See the [LayerDrop paper](see https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.11556) for more details. decoder_layerdrop (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.0): The LayerDrop probability for the decoder. See the [LayerDrop paper](see https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.11556) for more details. use_cache (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `True`): Whether or not the model should return the last key/values attentions (not used by all models) Example: ```python >>> from transformers import LEDModel, LEDConfig >>> # Initializing a LED allenai/led-base-16384 style configuration >>> configuration = LEDConfig() >>> # Initializing a model from the allenai/led-base-16384 style configuration >>> model = LEDModel(configuration) >>> # Accessing the model configuration >>> configuration = model.config ```""" model_type = "transgenic" attribute_map = { "num_attention_heads": "encoder_attention_heads", "hidden_size": "d_model", "attention_probs_dropout_prob": "attention_dropout", "initializer_range": "init_std", } def __init__( self, vocab_size=272, max_encoder_position_embeddings=16384, max_decoder_position_embeddings=2048, encoder_layers=6, encoder_ffn_dim=3072, encoder_attention_heads=12, decoder_layers=6, decoder_ffn_dim=3072, decoder_attention_heads=12, encoder_layerdrop=0.0, decoder_layerdrop=0.1, use_cache=True, is_encoder_decoder=True, activation_function="gelu", d_model=768, dropout=0.1, attention_dropout=0.0, activation_dropout=0.0, init_std=0.02, decoder_start_token_id=2, classifier_dropout=0.0, pad_token_id=1, bos_token_id=0, eos_token_id=2, attention_window: Union[List[int], int] = [ 1024, 1024, 1024, 1024, 1024, 1024 ], encoder_model="InstaDeepAI/agro-nucleotide-transformer-1b", unlink=False, s_model="InstaDeepAI/segment_nt_multi_species", numSegClasses=14, do_segment = True, **kwargs, ): self.vocab_size = vocab_size self.max_encoder_position_embeddings = max_encoder_position_embeddings self.max_decoder_position_embeddings = max_decoder_position_embeddings self.d_model = d_model self.encoder_ffn_dim = encoder_ffn_dim self.encoder_layers = encoder_layers self.encoder_attention_heads = encoder_attention_heads

nodes.body_text: class TransgenicHyenaConfig(PretrainedConfig): r""" This is the configuration class to store the configuration of a [`transgenicModel`]. It is used to instantiate an Transgenic model according to the specified arguments, defining the model architecture. Instantiating a configuration with the defaults will yield a similar configuration to that of the LED [jlomas/transgenic-agro-E9](https://huggingface.co/jlomas/transgenic-agro-E9) architecture. Configuration objects inherit from [`PretrainedConfig`] and can be used to control the model outputs. Read the documentation from [`PretrainedConfig`] for more information. Args: vocab_size (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 272): Vocabulary size of the Transgenic model. Defines the number of different tokens that can be represented by the `decoder_inputs_ids` passed when calling [`transgenicModel`]. d_model (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 1024): Dimensionality of the layers and the pooler layer. encoder_layers (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 12): Number of encoder layers. decoder_layers (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 12): Number of decoder layers. encoder_attention_heads (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 16): Number of attention heads for each attention layer in the Transformer encoder. decoder_attention_heads (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 16): Number of attention heads for each attention layer in the Transformer decoder. decoder_ffn_dim (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 4096): Dimensionality of the "intermediate" (often named feed-forward) layer in decoder. encoder_ffn_dim (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 4096): Dimensionality of the "intermediate" (often named feed-forward) layer in decoder. activation_function (`str` or `function`, *optional*, defaults to `"gelu"`): The non-linear activation function (function or string) in the encoder and pooler. If string, `"gelu"`, `"relu"`, `"silu"` and `"gelu_new"` are supported. dropout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.1): The dropout probability for all fully connected layers in the embeddings, encoder, and pooler. attention_dropout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.0): The dropout ratio for the attention probabilities. activation_dropout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.0): The dropout ratio for activations inside the fully connected layer. classifier_dropout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.0): The dropout ratio for classifier. max_encoder_position_embeddings (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 16384): The maximum sequence length that the encoder might ever be used with. max_decoder_position_embeddings (`int`, *optional*, defaults to 16384): The maximum sequence length that the decoder might ever be used with. init_std (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.02): The standard deviation of the truncated_normal_initializer for initializing all weight matrices. encoder_layerdrop (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.0): The LayerDrop probability for the encoder. See the [LayerDrop paper](see https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.11556) for more details. decoder_layerdrop (`float`, *optional*, defaults to 0.0): The LayerDrop probability for the decoder. See the [LayerDrop paper](see https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.11556) for more details. use_cache (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `True`): Whether or not the model should return the last key/values attentions (not used by all models) Example: ```python >>> from transformers import LEDModel, LEDConfig >>> # Initializing a LED allenai/led-base-16384 style configuration >>> configuration = LEDConfig() >>> # Initializing a model from the allenai/led-base-16384 style configuration >>> model = LEDModel(configuration) >>> # Accessing the model configuration >>> configuration = model.config ```""" model_type = "transgenicHyena" attribute_map = { "num_attention_heads": "encoder_attention_heads", "hidden_size": "d_model", "attention_probs_dropout_prob": "attention_dropout", "initializer_range": "init_std", } def __init__( self, vocab_size=272, max_encoder_position_embeddings=16384, max_decoder_position_embeddings=2048, encoder_layers=6, encoder_ffn_dim=3072, encoder_attention_heads=4, decoder_layers=9, decoder_ffn_dim=3072, decoder_attention_heads=4, encoder_layerdrop=0.0, decoder_layerdrop=0.1, use_cache=True, is_encoder_decoder=True, activation_function="gelu", d_model=256, dropout=0.1, attention_dropout=0.0, activation_dropout=0.0, init_std=0.02, decoder_start_token_id=2, classifier_dropout=0.0, pad_token_id=1, bos_token_id=0, eos_token_id=2, attention_window: Union[List[int], int] = [ 1024, 1024, 1024, 1024, 1024, 1024 ], encoder_model="LongSafari/hyenadna-large-1m-seqlen-hf", max_encoder_seqlen=49152, encoder_n_layer=9, unlink=False, s_model="InstaDeepAI/segment_nt_multi_species", numSegClasses=9, do_segment = False, **kwargs, ): self.vocab_size = vocab_size self.max_encoder_position_embeddings = max_encoder_position_embeddings self.max_decoder_position_embeddings = max_decoder_position_embeddings self.d_model = d_model self.encoder_ffn_dim = encoder_ffn_dim self.encoder_layers = encoder_layers self.e

nodes.name: createDenoisingLabel
nodes.signature: def createDenoisingLabel(pred, true): # Parse GSF strings
nodes.body_text: def createDenoisingLabel(pred, true): # Parse GSF strings true_features = [feat.split("|") for feat in true.split(">")[0].split(";")] true_transcripts = [set(feat.split("|")) for feat in true.split(">")[1].split(";")] pred_features = [feat.split("|") for feat in pred.split(">")[0].split(";")] pred_transcripts = [set(feat.split("|")) for feat in pred.split(">")[1].split(";")] # Set up feature index dictionaries for lookup true_fid = {} for i, feature in enumerate(true_features): true_fid[feature[1]] = i pred_fid = {} for i, feature in enumerate(pred_features): pred_fid[feature[1]] = i # Identify structurally matched transcripts matches = [] match_type = None for i,p in enumerate(pred_transcripts): for j, t in enumerate(true_transcripts): if p == t: matches.append([i,j]) if match_type != "CDS": match_type = "Full" else: p = {x for x in p if "CDS" in x} t = {x for x in t if "CDS" in x} if p==t: matches.append([i,j]) match_type = "CDS" if matches == []: return None # Create label (corrected prediction) label_features = copy.deepcopy(pred_features) mask_features = [] for p,t in matches: for feat in true_transcripts[t]: if (match_type == "CDS") & ("CDS" not in feat): continue label_features[pred_fid[feat]][0] = true_features[true_fid[feat]][0] # Start coord label_features[pred_fid[feat]][2] = true_features[true_fid[feat]][2] # End coord label_features[pred_fid[feat]][4] = true_features[true_fid[feat]][4] # Phase mask_features.append(feat) mask_features = set(mask_features) # Re-tokenize label = ";".join(["|".join(i) for i in label_features]) + ">" + pred.split(">")[1] tokenized_label = dt.batch_encode_plus( [label], return_tensors="pt", padding=True, truncation=True, add_special_tokens=True, max_length=2048) # Create mask for features with ground truth labels tokenized_mask_features = torch.tensor(dt.encode("|".join(list(mask_features)))[1:-1]) tokens_to_mask_inverse = torch.tensor(list(range(4,17))) feature_transcript_split = torch.nonzero(tokenized_label["input_ids"] == 17, as_tuple=True)[1][0] splits_indices = torch.nonzero(tokenized_label["input_ids"] == 21, as_tuple=True)[1] splits_indices = splits_indices[splits_indices < feature_transcript_split] mlm_mask = copy.deepcopy(tokenized_label["attention_mask"]) == False prev_split = 0 for split in splits_indices: id_section = tokenized_label["input_ids"][:, int(prev_split):int(split)] if torch.isin(id_section, tokenized_mask_features).sum() > 0: mlm_mask[:, prev_split:split] = torch.isin(id_section, tokens_to_mask_inverse) prev_split = split return (label, mlm_mask)
